nodes.label: annotate-source Skill
nodes.rationale: The platform's canonical data-model step: @annotate(concept, grain, roles, links) on each dlt resource drives staging generation, PII policy, monitors, metric candidates and graph edges. validate_annotations enforces concrete concepts, legal topology edges, money_amount/currency_code pairing, exactly one key column. nodes.label: find-source Skill
nodes.rationale: No hosted connector catalogue in dlt Core, so a three-tier ladder: verified sources (dlt init), OpenAPI-generated rest_api (dlt-init-openapi), hand-rolled rest_api. Always annotate, commit the connector back to the registry, never inline credentials. After first load, pf semantic scan induces an ontology proposal; the scan proposes, a human decides.

nodes.label: steward-ontology Skill
nodes.rationale: Induction proposes vocabulary; the human steward makes the four judgements induction cannot: synonym detection (minting a synonym silently splits every downstream metric), business verb naming, PII confirmation (never pre-accepted at any confidence; a missing tag fails loudly which is the safer failure), and specialisation via parent. Approved terms go to the group's extension.yaml only; another company never inherits a word that means nothing to them.

nodes.label: optimize-performance Skill
nodes.rationale: Diagnose before tuning via get_local_pipeline_state and load timings; symptom-to-lever table (parallelized extract, buffer/file rotation for memory, parquet loader format, load workers). Full reload every run usually means missing incremental. Never raise concurrency past the project's DuckDB writer pool.

nodes.label: setup-data-quality Skill
nodes.rationale: Two layers catch different failures: deterministic schema contracts at load time (DEFAULT_CONTRACT evolves tables/columns but freezes data_type; STRICT_CONTRACT for mature sources) and statistical monitors after load, generated from ontology roles by monitors_for, never hand-written. dbt tests catch nulls and duplicates; monitors catch the failure that costs money.

nodes.label: install-duckdb Skill
nodes.rationale: One pinned extension set (httpfs, json, spatial, excel) auto-loaded in Warehouse.connect. Adding an extension is a platform change affecting every company -- propose it, never apply from a project session; community extensions need explicit security review.

nodes.label: read-file Skill
nodes.rationale: Profile a data file before scaffolding a pipeline -- guessing a schema is how a filesystem source ends up all-VARCHAR. The profile (columns, types, null rates, keys, timestamps, money columns) feeds the pipeline scaffold and becomes the annotation roles.

nodes.label: read-memories Skill
nodes.rationale: Memories are scoped per-project on purpose: session logs stay inside the project so recovering context can never leak a sister's business logic. Prefer the context card and knowledge graph over log archaeology; reach for memories when the question is 'why was it done this way', which the graph cannot answer. Promotion into group or platform rules is a reviewed human step.

nodes.label: build-dashboard Skill
nodes.rationale: Start from the metric, never the chart; pick the chart form by the data's job; compose to the standard page anatomy; colour by job from the theme only. Non-negotiables: no dual-axis charts, selective labelling, one question per page. Adapted from the vendored evidence-bi upstream skill pack.

nodes.label: dashboard-loop Skill
nodes.rationale: Iterative draft-score-critique-fix loop that terminates because most of the quality bar is mechanically checkable by pf report audit; judgement questions are asked once per pass, not re-litigated. A pass that changes nothing is the signal to stop, not to look harder; rejected options are recorded in decisions/ so the next pass does not re-litigate them.

Read the vendored Forge skill pack's props before writing a component: wss3-forge exports 358 names and guessed props fail to compile. theme.css adds only what a data console needs and Forge has no opinion about: monospace identifiers, tabular numerals, shared verdict colours.

nodes.label: Contributing Guide
nodes.rationale: Structural rules are stricter than most projects because the platform is multi-tenant and its audit trail is part of the product.

nodes.label: Vendor Directory Read-Only Rule
nodes.rationale: The 21 upstreams are pinned as submodules for provenance; what was adopted from each is recorded in platform/src/pf/vendor/registry.yaml. Bumping a pin is a maintainer decision made through the weekly sync PR, never part of a feature change.

nodes.label: Entity Isolation Rule
nodes.rationale: Business logic under groups/<group>/projects/<project>/ belongs to one entity. An assumption carried across entities is a bug, not a refactor — never copy logic between groups or sister projects.

nodes.label: Append-Only Provenance Rule
nodes.rationale: The action record in provenance/ is append-only and written by the platform's hooks; pf provenance verify blocks CI if the chain is broken. Agents may not edit the record of what they did.

nodes.label: Security Policy
nodes.rationale: Pre-1.0: only the latest commit on main is supported. Vulnerabilities are reported privately by email, never as public issues.

nodes.label: Provenance Tampering In Scope
nodes.rationale: Findings that allow tampering with or bypassing the hash-chained provenance log (provenance/, docs/GOVERNANCE.md) are in scope and treated as high severity — the audit trail is part of the product.

nodes.label: Credentials Live In The Environment
nodes.rationale: Credentials live only in the environment (.env, dlt secrets.toml) — never in the repository. A committed secret is itself a reportable finding.

nodes.label: Third-Party Notices
nodes.rationale: Apache-2.0 repo pinning 21 upstreams as read-only submodules. Submodules are pointers, not copies — cloning without --recurse-submodules fetches no upstream code. The authoritative per-path record of every borrowing is platform/src/pf/vendor/registry.yaml (pf vendor list -v, pf vendor why <file>).

nodes.label: FINOS AI Governance Framework
nodes.rationale: CC BY 4.0 control/risk catalogue and mitigation vocabularies, read at runtime and partially copied into pf.air; credit line emitted in every generated register (pf/air/sources.py).

nodes.label: OpenTopology
nodes.rationale: Apache-2.0. Relationship vocabulary taken verbatim (governed_by, implemented_by, verified_by); schema validated against in place, never copied.

nodes.label: WrenAI
nodes.rationale: MDL field names and cardinality enum taken from core/ (Apache-2.0). Tri-licensed with a pre-emptive AGPL-3.0: no path is AGPL yet, but a vendor pin bump moving paths onto AGPL-3.0 is the event to watch for — the drift gate (pf vendor drift) is the mechanism that surfaces it.

nodes.label: Recce Vendor Family
nodes.rationale: recce (Apache-2.0), recce-ui (Apache-2.0) and recce-pr-update (MIT) are pinned for contract, drift-watch or CLI invocation only — no material adapted into this repo.

nodes.label: recce-claude-plugin Licence Gap
nodes.rationale: Declares no license (verified against the GitHub API 2026-08-19), so default is all-rights-reserved and the ported recce-review skill is a derivative of unlicensed content. Sibling repos are Apache-2.0/MIT so this reads as upstream oversight; fix is an upstream licence request or an independent rewrite. Tracked in registry.yaml under licence_review.

nodes.label: loop-engineering
nodes.rationale: MIT. Loop building blocks adapted into pf/loops/.

nodes.label: asqav-compliance ELv2 Constraint
nodes.rationale: Elastic License 2.0, executed unmodified from its submodule in CI. ELv2 forbids providing the software as a managed service: the platform must not expose the scanner as a compliance-scanning feature to its own tenants. Recorded in registry.yaml under licence_review.

nodes.label: dlthub-ai-workbench
nodes.rationale: Proprietary dltHub License. No source copied — the dlt toolkits are independent rewrites against dlt Core's public Apache-2.0 API. Standing note: confirm scope-of-use with counsel.

nodes.label: Per-Project DuckDB Writer Pools
nodes.rationale: Every writing asset is tagged with a per-project pool (duckdb_writer_<project>) limited to 1, letting sister companies run in parallel while respecting DuckDB's single-writer lock. Granularity must be op, not run: run granularity serialises whole runs but lets every step inside one run execute at once — the three dlt ingest assets fired concurrently and collided on the single-writer lock. runs and pools must both live under concurrency as of Dagster 1.13.

nodes.label: Claude Review Workflow
nodes.rationale: Deliberately label-gated (add the claude-review label) rather than running on every PR: it is billed per Anthropic API run, and the checks that must always happen already run unconditionally elsewhere — this one is for reviews needing judgement rather than a rule. The platform's own verdicts (pf gate, pf check) go into the prompt as evidence; Claude reviews what a rule cannot decide, and disagreeing with the gate is itself a finding. Review criteria: SQL semantics, semantic-layer drift, unmentioned blast radius, entity isolation, secrets/PII. Missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY exits with an explanation rather than failing red. Review only — no file modification.

nodes.label: PR Impact Report Workflow
nodes.rationale: Every PR gets one impact report comment edited in place — a thread of eleven stale reports is how a reviewer learns to ignore the bot. The same JSON is uploaded as an artifact so pf ui shows the verdict CI computed instead of recomputing and disagreeing. Submodules are fetched with --depth 1 --filter=blob:none, never via checkout's fetch-depth: 0 + submodules: recursive, which full-clones every upstream — that combination wedged PR #201 in actions/checkout for twelve hours and held the concurrency group. pf vendor drift degrades visibly ('<id> not checked out') on a partial fetch. Verdict enforcement is a separate step from posting, so the report is visible whether or not it blocks.

nodes.label: Control Plane Stack
nodes.rationale: OpenMetadata, Dagster and recce on one database, one origin (nginx at :8080) and one image — everything above the database line runs in one container, pf_stack, while Postgres and Elasticsearch stay separate because folding a database into an application image is how you lose the database. PF_REPO must be the repo root and is bind-mounted at its host path, because Dagster's workspace holds absolute working_directory entries. Code servers are standalone grpc_server processes (a python_module entry forks per-location children in both webserver and daemon — 19 processes, 3.1 GB); recce servers (~350 MB each) start only where there is a review. Recce state lives in R2 via pf artifacts, not in a database.

nodes.label: One Database, Two Schemas
nodes.rationale: openmetadata_db holds OpenMetadata (public, ~176 tables) and Dagster (dagster schema, owned by a role with no rights in public). Dagster has no schema setting, so search_path is urlencoded onto the libpq connection string via params/options. Dropping that one parameter does not fail — Dagster's migrations run happily against public, interleaving tables with OpenMetadata's, and the damage only shows at the next OpenMetadata upgrade. Unset PF_STACK_PG_HOST means SQLite, and pf stack render removes the storage block entirely rather than pointing at an unreachable Postgres, which would fail at import and take every code location down.

nodes.label: Path-Based Origin Merge
nodes.rationale: OpenMetadata's UI and recce's UI are both root-anchored SPAs; recce's Next.js static export has no basePath so a path-prefixed proxy renders its 404. The merge happens on paths instead: /api/v1/ is OpenMetadata's API, /api/ is recce's, and nginx's ^~ on /api/v1/ is the one rule holding the two APIs apart. /recce/<project> sets a pf_recce cookie that an nginx map turns into a port — one project in view at a time, which is what a review is. The injected navigation bar loads via sub_filter from /pf/bar.css and /pf/bar.js because OpenMetadata's CSP would drop an inline script. Stated cost: root routes /lineage, /checks, /query now belong to recce.

nodes.label: Self-Decrypting Catalogue Credential
nodes.rationale: catalog_sync authenticates to OpenMetadata as the ingestion bot. Inside the stack the publisher and server share a database and FERNET_KEY, so the entrypoint decrypts the bot's JWT from user_entity once at start and exports it — a credential nobody typed, held in the process environment and written nowhere. An explicit OPENMETADATA_JWT_TOKEN still wins, so a narrower bot or remote catalogue is never silently replaced; outside the stack the env var remains the only source. Upstream trap: OpenMetadata 1.13.3's Postgres DDL generates isbot from json->>'deleted', so the bot flag is read out of the JSON instead.

nodes.label: pf Platform dbt Project
nodes.rationale: Minimal platform-level dbt project whose only job is exposing shared macros via macro-paths.

nodes.label: Control Plane Compose Stack
nodes.rationale: Three containers where there were five: postgresql (one database, two schemas), elasticsearch (OpenMetadata search index), and a combined stack image (OpenMetadata + Dagster + recce + nginx). PF_REPO must mount at the same path as on the host because Dagster's workspace.yaml holds absolute working_directory paths.

nodes.label: pf_postgresql Service
nodes.rationale: Pinned independently of OM_VERSION: following OpenMetadata's postgresql tag looks tidy but a Postgres major bump would meet the old data directory and refuse to start, taking both OpenMetadata and Dagster (same instance) down. Loopback-only publish; dev database with a published default password.

nodes.label: pf_elasticsearch Service
nodes.rationale: Independent of OM_VERSION for the opposite reason: OpenMetadata constrains which Elasticsearch majors it talks to, so this may need to move with an upgrade (PF_OM_REINDEX=recreate). Heap trimmed to 512m — the index holds ~1200 tables and a glossary; 1g starved the stack beside it.

nodes.label: pf_stack Service (OpenMetadata + Dagster + recce + nginx)
nodes.rationale: One combined image. OpenMetadata uses the public schema and Dagster the dagster schema of the same openmetadata_db. Own DAGSTER_HOME (.dagster-stack), not the repo's .dagster, so the host's instance config never names a database it cannot reach. Credentials come from .env, never baked into the image.

nodes.label: External Volumes Fail Loudly
nodes.rationale: Volumes are external on purpose: they hold the previous hand-started OpenMetadata stack's 1205 catalogued tables and search index. A compose-owned volume would silently start empty; external: true fails loudly if missing.

nodes.label: Party (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: Abstract: any actor that can enter into an agreement.

nodes.label: Customer (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A party that buys; person or organization. Identity: customer_id.

nodes.label: Organization (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A legal entity; customers may belong to one.

nodes.label: Employee (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: Internal actor, used for attribution.

nodes.label: Agreement (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: Abstract: a commitment between parties, with a lifecycle.

nodes.label: Subscription (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A recurring agreement with a plan, term and status.

nodes.label: Order (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A one-off purchase commitment.

nodes.label: Contract (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A negotiated agreement, usually with custom terms.

nodes.label: Event (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: Abstract: something that happened at a point in time. Immutable.

nodes.label: Payment (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: Movement of money settling an agreement.

nodes.label: Refund (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: Negative movement of money against a prior payment.

nodes.label: Usage (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: Metered consumption attributable to an agreement.

nodes.label: Interaction (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A touchpoint (email, call, session) with a party.

nodes.label: Product (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A sellable thing; plans and SKUs are Products.

nodes.label: Location (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: A geography: country, region, or address.

nodes.label: Currency (ontology class)
nodes.rationale: An ISO 4217 currency; qualifies every money amount.

nodes.label: Platform Ontology v2
nodes.rationale: v2 adds identity (which property identifies an instance — without it no join condition can be derived, so BI and MDL projections are guesses) and datatype properties on the class itself. Kept deliberately small: a 200-class upper ontology nobody maintains is worse than 15 classes everybody uses; groups select a subset in instance.yaml.

nodes.label: Column Semantic Roles
nodes.rationale: Every annotated column carries exactly one role. Each role's `review` intent (identity / distribution / categories / none) is tool-agnostic: the ontology states the question, each review tool translates it. Strings must declare whether they are categories or free text — guessing wrong makes every review noisy. pii: true forces review none, because a value-level diff would persist real PII into a durable shared state file.

nodes.label: Microsoft Ontology-Playground
nodes.rationale: External reference modelling the same class + datatype-property and OWL object-property pairs.

nodes.label: Topology v2 (Named Relations)
nodes.rationale: Replaces the flat from/to edge list with four load-bearing changes: relation names (MDL requires relationships[].name), OWL domain/range framing, MDL's cardinality enum verbatim (a '1:N' string needed translating, and translation is where direction gets silently flipped), and an inverse name so every relation reads both ways. The physical join condition is deliberately NOT here — derived at projection time from each project's links_to annotations, keeping the topology warehouse-independent.

nodes.label: MDL (WrenAI Modeling Definition Language)
nodes.rationale: The projection target for the semantic layer: requires named relationships and understands the ONE_TO_ONE | ONE_TO_MANY | MANY_TO_ONE | MANY_TO_MANY cardinality enum verbatim.

nodes.label: Control Plane Web Entry (Vite/React)
nodes.rationale: Minimal Vite entry mounting /src/main.tsx into #root; same 'Data Platform — Control Plane' title as the single-file static UI.

nodes.label: Skill: build-assets (Dagster)
nodes.rationale: Never scaffold a Definitions object — a second Definitions silently shadows the factory's resources and is the most likely way to break the repo. The pipeline builds itself: sources/, dbt models and sisters maps are auto-discovered; definitions.py never changes after scaffolding. dbt models emit one asset per model, never one shelled-out dbt build — one opaque asset produces a node with no edges. Asset keys are project-prefixed because sisters have identically-named models across code locations. Adapted from dagster-io/skills (Apache-2.0).

nodes.label: Skill: contracts-and-access (dbt governance)
nodes.rationale: Contracts, groups, access and versions are dbt Core features — use them. access: private on staging/intermediate, public only on marts consumed outside the group. Mesh caveat: cross-project ref is dbt Cloud only — here the boundary is the project; sisters do not ref each other, cross-entity data flows through _rollup via ATTACH READ_ONLY. Declare exposures for every dashboard or impact analysis cannot name an owner.

nodes.label: Skill: troubleshoot-runs
nodes.rationale: No Cloud Jobs API; the equivalents are run_results.json (failed_nodes) and the Dagster run log. Classify before fixing: upstream_data / model_logic / stale_source / test_too_strict — 're-run it' is only correct for stale_source. A test that fails because the test is wrong is a real outcome; say so rather than contorting the model.

nodes.label: Skill: fetch-docs
nodes.rationale: Prefer the local manifest over the internet; this is dbt Core + dbt-duckdb + MetricFlow CLI, so ignore dbt Cloud-only guidance (Semantic Layer API, Discovery API, Jobs API, cross-project ref) — the local equivalents are mf query, manifest.json, run_results.json and per-project isolation.

nodes.label: Skill: run-commands
nodes.rationale: Always run dbt via dbt_build/dbt_test/dbt_list so target and PF_DUCKDB_PATH are wired. state:modified+ is the CI selector and the input to impact analysis. Never --full-refresh from a chat turn — destructive operations go through pf plan → human review → pf apply.

nodes.label: dbt Layer Boundaries
nodes.rationale: staging owns cleaning (never joins, aggregation, grain changes); intermediate owns joins and reshaping (never exposed to BI); marts own grain and the physical table (never an aggregation policy); semantic owns metric definitions (never stores data). Enforced in review, and agents blur them constantly.

nodes.label: Skill: answer-with-metrics
nodes.rationale: The Cloud Semantic Layer API does not exist here; the equivalent is the MetricFlow CLI wrapped as query_metrics. If no metric covers the question, say so and name the missing definition — that gap report is how the semantic layer grows from real questions. Recomputing a defined metric in ad-hoc SQL is how one company ends up with four different revenues. Always state which metric and filter were used.

nodes.label: Skill: build-semantic-layer
nodes.rationale: The mart declares the grain; the semantic layer declares how to aggregate it. Derive agg_time_dimension from the column annotated event_time and measures from money_amount/quantity. Ratio and derived metrics compose existing metrics — never recompute a numerator in SQL. saved_queries with exports keep BI tables derived from the single definition.

nodes.label: dbt-snowflake Toolkit (portable sf_* macros)
nodes.rationale: Snowflake functions as dbt macros compiling to whatever the target adapter understands, so one set of models runs on DuckDB in development and Snowflake in production. The macros reproduce the SOURCE dialect's semantics, not the local warehouse's: sf_least returns NULL if any argument is NULL, sf_div0 returns 0 on a zero divisor, sf_datediff takes the part first. Each is asserted against a real dbt run. The sf_ prefix names the dialect the SQL came from; a BigQuery-origin project gets a sibling bq_* toolkit.

nodes.label: Ambiguous Dialect Functions
nodes.rationale: Functions whose meaning depends on which dialect wrote them are deliberately never translated automatically: date_trunc is (part, date) in Snowflake and (date, part) in BigQuery — both parse, one returns wrong dates silently. Listed in AMBIGUOUS in pf/onboard/dialect.py and reported by pf dialect for a human to resolve, because a wrong argument order compiles, runs, and produces numbers no review catches.

nodes.label: Skill: port-snowflake-sql
nodes.rationale: Start with the pf dialect report, not the SQL. Work ambiguous first and by hand (nothing fails, so nothing tells you), then the mechanical needs-wrapping pile (loud, cheap), then unsupported. Macro arguments are quoted SQL fragments — a bare identifier renders empty and fails to compile, the good kind of failure. Do not wrap what dbt-core already handles. New macros must pin the source dialect's answer in test_toolkit_macros.py.

nodes.label: Skill: add-tests
nodes.rationale: Generate tests from annotations rather than by hand — roles already declare intent (natural_key → unique + not_null, foreign_key → relationships, status_enum → accepted_values...). Severity deliberate: error on key/referential, warn on distribution; a test that always warns and is never fixed is noise. transform/tests/expectations/ is the generated floor — fix the role, never the file. A rule that cannot be written down is a monitor, not a test.

nodes.label: Skill: add-unit-test
nodes.rationale: Data tests check the output of a real run; unit tests check the logic against fixed inputs, catching a broken CASE branch current data never hits. Write one for every model encoding a business rule, and test-drive it: failing unit test first, then the SQL.
nodes.community_name: Skills Add Unit Test — Skill: Add-Unit-Test

nodes.label: Skill: explore-data
nodes.rationale: Order: list_tables → display_schema → preview_table → aggregate with execute_sql_query. Read-only and truncated by policy; if capped, aggregate in SQL rather than asking for more rows. Stop and re-route to query_metrics if the question is a business-metric question. Notebooks read the project DuckDB file read-only and never write to the warehouse.

nodes.label: Stripe Connector Registry Entry
nodes.rationale: Verified source stripe_analytics; maps charges to Payment, customers to Customer, subscriptions to Subscription, all incremental on created. Notes: amounts arrive in minor units (divide by 100 in staging); Stripe status enum drifts when new states are added, caught by the status_enum monitor.

nodes.label: DuckDB Single-Writer Constraint
nodes.rationale: DuckDB allows a single writer per database file. This constraint is why the platform gives every project its own file and its own Dagster writer pool -- it is what makes sister companies genuinely parallel. Never propose a shared file for multiple writers.

nodes.label: elementary-observe Toolkit Context
nodes.rationale: Every dbt build records itself into main_elementary (the elementary tool is on by default); these skills are how that recording gets used rather than merely collected.

nodes.label: Test vs Monitor Distinction
nodes.rationale: A test asserts a rule; a monitor learns a baseline from history and flags departures. Add monitors exactly where a rule cannot be written down (volumes, freshness, distributions). Anomaly monitors are severity: warn because an anomaly is a question, not a verdict -- a monitor that pages on every marketing campaign gets deleted.

nodes.label: add-anomaly-tests Skill
nodes.rationale: Monitors are chosen from the ontology role, not guessed: event_time gives timestamp_column, the table gets volume_anomalies, status_enum/geo/booleans get dimension_anomalies, money_amount gets column_anomalies, contract-critical tables get schema_changes. Declared in the model's own yml because it is a judgement about one table. Build twice before trusting -- first build passes vacuously. Never monitor a PII column's values: value-level metrics would put real values into the durable shared main_elementary schema.

nodes.label: triage-observability Skill
nodes.rationale: Triage queries the recorded history (main_elementary tables), not the log of whichever run failed: one failure is an incident, the history says whether it is new, recurring or flaky, and those get different fixes. Verdicts: upstream_data, model_logic, stale_source, test_too_strict, expected_anomaly. An anomaly you cannot classify is a finding -- report it as unexplained. A monitor acknowledged every week is a broken monitor or an unowned problem.

nodes.label: Immutable Record Principle
nodes.rationale: Never edit main_elementary tables or transform/edr_target: the record of what happened is gate-denied for the same reason provenance/** is -- you may not edit the record of what you did. The report is regenerated, never patched.

nodes.label: Metric-First Reporting Principle
nodes.rationale: Every number on a page traces to a metric in queries/metrics/. A figure with no metric is a metric PR, not page SQL.

nodes.label: Ratio Re-Division Rule
nodes.rationale: Never avg(ratio). Ratio queries carry numerator and denominator so pages re-divide at their own grain: sum(num)/sum(den).

nodes.label: Status Never Colour Alone
nodes.rationale: Every verdict renders a dot and the word (see src/components/Verdict.tsx): screenshots get printed and pasted into tickets, and roughly one reader in twelve cannot separate the red from the green.

nodes.label: A Zero Is Not a Result
nodes.rationale: Distinguish 'checked, found nothing' from 'nothing checked it'. A green nought over an unmeasured project is a clean bill of health nobody issued.
nodes.norm_label: a zero is not a result

nodes.label: Entity Isolation Principle
nodes.rationale: Never read another group or a sister project; cross-entity work happens only in _rollup. Business logic does not transfer between entities -- an assumption carried across is a bug.

nodes.label: Graph-Before-Files Principle
nodes.rationale: kg_search costs a few hundred tokens; reading four models to find the same edge costs thousands and is likelier to be wrong. impact_analysis before changing any column, model or metric.

nodes.label: Read-Only Verifier Principle
nodes.rationale: The verification subagents are read-only by construction: a verifier that can edit stops being a second opinion and becomes a second author. If one finds a fault, it reports; the main session fixes.

nodes.label: Found-None vs No-Impact Distinction
nodes.rationale: Never say 'no impact' when what you mean is 'I found none' -- state which one it is. An empty result from an empty or stale graph is not evidence; compare the graph's mtime against the newest model file and declare the verification incomplete if stale.

nodes.label: secrets-auditor agent
nodes.rationale: Read-only subagent that hunts leaked credentials and PII; never prints a secret it finds, only location and shape, so the report is safe to paste into a ticket.

nodes.label: Exposed / Exposable / Placeholder triage
nodes.rationale: Remediation differs by class: exposed credentials must be rotated before removal because deleting a file does not un-expose git history; exposable paths need the gate rule fixed before the next run collects secrets; placeholders are named explicitly so nobody re-audits them.

nodes.label: semantic-conformance agent
nodes.rationale: Checks that the semantic claims a project makes are still true — not whether the SQL runs, but whether what it says it means holds. Unverifiable is a legitimate result; silence about it is not.

nodes.label: Semantic chain: ontology to annotation to model to metric to contract
nodes.rationale: Meaning flows link by link; break any link and everything downstream is decoration. A resource annotated after models were written has causality backwards — meaning reverse-engineered from models rather than models derived from meaning.
nodes.norm_label: semantic chain: ontology to annotation to model to metric to contract

nodes.label: Conformed dimensions belong to the group
nodes.rationale: Two sisters with private definitions of the same dimension will eventually disagree about a customer and neither will be obviously wrong; a local re-implementation is a finding — compare against the group, never a sister project.
nodes.norm_label: conformed dimensions belong to the group

nodes.label: sql-reviewer agent
nodes.rationale: Reviews compiled dbt SQL (not the Jinja) for correctness faults, ranked by how often each is actually wrong; every finding names the wrong answer it produces as a concrete scenario, with a query that demonstrates the fault and passes after the fix.

nodes.label: Grain uniqueness verification
nodes.rationale: A mart whose declared meta.grain is not unique is the single most common cause of double-counted metrics downstream. Verify with select grain, count(*) group by all having count(*) > 1 rather than trusting the declaration.

nodes.label: Faults that produce wrong numbers without erroring
nodes.rationale: The dangerous fault class errors nowhere: join fanout multiplying rows before aggregates, an inner join silently dropping rows, a left join with a where on the right table acting as inner, not-in with a nullable subquery returning no rows, a wrong incremental unique_key corrupting data over time rather than failing once.
nodes.norm_label: faults that produce wrong numbers without erroring

nodes.label: Architecture as checkable claims
nodes.rationale: In this platform architecture is not a diagram but a set of claims the graph can check; review means finding the claims that are no longer true.

nodes.label: Declared joins (links plus topology)
nodes.rationale: Every foreign key must be declared as links={col: SomeClass} AND the topology must already relate the two classes — one without the other is the common half-failure where nothing is derivable. An undeclared join is a join whose condition was guessed; pf check fails on it, the highest-value signal in the review.

nodes.label: /ast-grep command
nodes.rationale: Structural, syntax-aware search for when regex would match the wrong thing. Not installed by default — say so and fall back to Grep rather than silently degrading. Scope to one project or platform/; a bare dot walks vendor/ and .venv and crosses entity boundaries. The graph outranks both search tools for dependency questions.

nodes.label: Blast radius / impact_analysis
nodes.rationale: pf impact / impact_analysis reports downstream reach, not a verdict. The dangerous class is metrics: a metric depending on a changed column changes value silently — nothing errors, the number is just different. Changes reaching published contracts (mdl.json, openmetadata.json) affect external consumers and must be announced, not just merged.

nodes.label: Empty blast radius trichotomy
nodes.rationale: An empty result means one of three non-equivalent things: nothing depends on it (proceed), the graph lacks the node (rebuild and re-ask), or there is no graph at all — then the gate is inert and every edit is unverified. Never treat silence as safety.

nodes.label: Enforced context budget (pf tokens)
nodes.rationale: Over budget is a build failure, not a warning, because every session pays the preamble for the whole life of the project. Repair by regenerating the card, not trimming by hand; if still over, the fix is fewer better entries, not a bigger budget.

nodes.label: Graph queries instead of file reads
nodes.rationale: The cheapest large-context strategy is not loading the context: kg_neighbors instead of reading four models, kg_search instead of grepping for a concept, impact_analysis instead of reading downstream models — and never reading a sister project at all.
nodes.norm_label: graph queries instead of file reads

nodes.label: /gemini-analyze command
nodes.rationale: Hands a repo-sized question to Gemini's large context window instead of compacting the session. Read-only; never include secrets since @ inlines file contents into a third-party request. Treat output as a lead, not a finding — verify each claim against the file it names.

nodes.label: Large-context delegation scope rule
nodes.rationale: Run gemini from the active project directory and never pass @ paths reaching another group or sister; --all_files from the repo root sweeps every entity — exactly the cross-entity read the gate exists to prevent — and drags vendor/ and .venv into the prompt.

nodes.label: Measure before recommending
nodes.rationale: dbt already recorded the timing in run_results.json — read it, do not re-run. The top three slowest rows are the audit; everything below them is noise until those are addressed. A plausible optimisation targeting the wrong stage is worse than none.

nodes.label: PII check on committed recce_state.json
nodes.rationale: The repo deliberately commits transform/recce_state.json, and value_diff checks write compared row values into it. That is only safe while PII columns (email, phone, name, address, dob, ssn, iban, card) stay excluded from those checks — a hit is critical because the values are already in git history.

nodes.label: Gate coverage as holes, not rules
nodes.rationale: The question is not what the gate denies but what it fails to deny: every generator-written artefact must be on the denylist (otherwise drift reappears as a hand edit the next regeneration discards silently), every denylist_except entry must be a deliberate still-true exception.
nodes.norm_label: gate coverage as holes, not rules

nodes.label: Ordered ship sequence
nodes.rationale: Each step produces the input for the next; a failure stops the sequence rather than being noted and passed over. A commit that does two things cannot be reverted for one of them. A denied path is not a thing to argue with; the pre-commit hook re-running the gate is right when it blocks — --no-verify is not part of this workflow.

nodes.label: Inert governance as the costliest debt
nodes.rationale: Debt in a data platform is mostly governance that went inert: a gate that cannot fire, a graph that no longer matches the models, a contract nobody regenerated. A stale graph is worse than none because it reports a blast radius that is wrong. Anything that makes a gate inert is silently disabling a control — the only debt that gets worse without being touched.
nodes.norm_label: inert governance as the costliest debt

nodes.label: project-onboarding rules
nodes.rationale: The toolkit's binding rules: the stage order is a dependency not a preference; implement addresses one finding per iteration; maker and checker must not be the same agent; three failures open a circuit breaker to escalate, never clear; never --force past a blocker except for a later stage's findings.

nodes.label: onboard-project skill
nodes.rationale: Onboarding is not a prompt, it is a loop you design and then run: adopting the files is cheap; making the project mean something — ontology, layers, metrics, review discipline — is the work. Names its own three failure modes: verification quietly becoming manual, comprehension debt, and cognitive surrender after the fortieth green check.

nodes.label: Gated onboarding ladder
nodes.rationale: import, ontology, dialect, layers, metrics, review — the order is a dependency: annotations cannot be written against SQL that will not compile, metrics cannot precede the marts they measure, recce cannot diff a project that never built. Out of order, every stage is redone when the one beneath it lands. pf align status re-derives every stage from disk and never reads a stored verdict, because a recorded pass outlives the change that invalidated it.

nodes.label: Maker/checker separation (validate vs verify)
nodes.rationale: validate asks is the project correct now; verify asks is the change that got it there one we would accept. Both must pass and they catch different things — a project passes every gate if you delete the failing test. The checker's default stance is no; it cannot check intent, so the implementing agent must never be the verifying agent.

nodes.label: Three-failure circuit breaker
nodes.rationale: Every validate result is written to loop-ledger.json; three consecutive failures of a stage open a breaker. Deliberate: an agent re-reading 'max three attempts' cannot know it is on the fourth, and a count held in conversation resets on restart. A finding that survived three implement phases is a decision someone has to make, not a bug being failed at — pf loop reset is for after the decision, not instead of it.

nodes.label: Unexercised is not a pass
nodes.rationale: unexercised is what a check reports when the tool that would decide it is not installed. Reporting it green is the difference between an onboarding that was verified and one that was assumed — yet it also must not close the gate, because a missing CLI must not wall a project off from the ladder.

nodes.label: Entity boundary rule
nodes.rationale: Never read another group or another sister project: business logic does not transfer between entities, and an assumption carried across is a bug that is invisible in review because it looks like knowledge. Escalate business meaning, never guess it — which of two revenue definitions a company means is not inferable from its SQL.

nodes.label: Stage 1: import
nodes.rationale: Goal: the repository is here, every model name is unique, no dbt built-in overridden. Deliberately leaves behind profiles.yml (the platform owns targets), generate_schema_name (its usual override collapses schemas and defeats the layer separation the graph and impact gate read), build artefacts, and unpinned unused packages. A new group asserts a shared ontology instance, conformed dimensions and a meaningful roll-up — folding an unrelated company in to save a directory is how conformed dimensions stop conforming.

nodes.label: Stage 2: ontology, topology, annotations
nodes.rationale: First for a reason: annotations drive generated staging, currency normalisation, PII policy, the knowledge graph, the MDL projection and the impact gate — modelling before annotating means modelling against a vocabulary nobody has agreed on yet. Roles are the contract; a mart is not annotated because that would give a definition two homes.

nodes.label: Ontology / topology / annotations split
nodes.rationale: Ontology (what kinds of thing exist) is warehouse-independent; topology names how kinds relate; the binding to physical columns lives only in per-project annotations — which is why the same topology serves sister companies whose tables look nothing alike.

nodes.label: Ontology proposal flow (scan / review / approve)
nodes.rationale: When the ontology has no word for it, do not force a bad fit — annotating a supplier as Organization makes the validator pass and every downstream projection wrong. pf semantic scan induces a proposal, review shows the diff, approve merges into the group extension (not the platform ontology) so a new concept reaches the sisters that need it without imposing on every company. Approving is a human decision.

nodes.label: Stage 3: dialect — one SQL, two targets
nodes.rationale: The same models compile on DuckDB in development and on the production warehouse and mean the same on both. Development is DuckDB because a developer who needs a warehouse account to run the project stops running the project. There are not two copies of the SQL — a per-warehouse fork diverges on the first bug fix.
nodes.norm_label: stage 3: dialect — one sql, two targets

nodes.label: Ambiguous cross-dialect functions
nodes.rationale: Two failure classes, not equally dangerous: unsupported functions (iff, nvl, div0) fail the build loudly and cost minutes; ambiguous ones compile and run on both sides and return a different number, costing a dashboard — least(1, NULL) is NULL in Snowflake and 1 in DuckDB, datediff and date_trunc swap argument order between dialects. Give the ambiguous findings the attention: they are already running and can already be wrong.

nodes.label: Portable sf_* dispatch macros
nodes.rationale: Macros from platform/toolkits/dbt-snowflake use adapter.dispatch so one call compiles to whatever the target understands — and they pin the source dialect's semantics everywhere, which is the point: sf_least(1, NULL) is NULL on DuckDB too. Three deliberately differ from DuckDB natives (sf_least, sf_div0, sf_safe_divide); do not 'fix' them. Missing macros are added from a platform session, never a project one.

nodes.label: Stage 4: layers — staging, marts, semantic
nodes.rationale: Goal: every model sits in the layer whose rules it obeys. intermediate/ maps to marts/ — not a demotion: an intermediate model is a mart nothing exposes yet, and internal-vs-published is a tag, not a directory. A join in staging hides a business decision in a layer the platform treats as mechanical, and gen-staging will overwrite it.

nodes.label: Four-layer contract (staging / marts / semantic / utils)
nodes.rationale: Each layer is a contract, not a folder: staging is 1:1 with raw (no joins, no aggregation), marts declare a grain, semantic is MetricFlow YAML only. The knowledge graph derives lineage depth from them, the PII audit only flags columns reaching a mart, the impact gate weighs mart changes more heavily, and the semantic layer treats marts/ as measurable — a model in the wrong layer is reasoned about wrongly by four different tools.

nodes.label: Config re-keying after directory moves
nodes.rationale: dbt_project.yml blocks are keyed by directory: after a move, a block naming a directory that no longer exists silently stops applying every tag under it — the build is green and the tags are gone. Verify by counting tagged nodes in the manifest, not by reading the YAML.

nodes.label: Stage 5: MetricFlow metrics
nodes.rationale: A mart nothing measures is a table. The semantic model binds a mart to entities, dimensions and measures — the ontology-stage annotations say which column is which: natural_key becomes the primary entity, links become foreign entities, event_time the agg_time_dimension, money_amount a measure.

nodes.label: One definition per business quantity
nodes.rationale: The point of the semantic layer is that revenue has exactly one definition — the alternative is two dashboards filtering differently and nobody able to say which is right. Compose (ratio, derived with offset) rather than recompute: recomputing is how the second definition gets in. Definitions come from the source repository's own KPI marts and analyses, cited in the description — inventing a revenue definition for a company onboarded this morning is exactly the guess the platform says to escalate.

nodes.label: Stage 6: Recce review
nodes.rationale: Goal: the difference between what was there and what is there now has been looked at. Look at row counts on every mart, then value diffs on the models wrapped in the dialect stage (the highest-yield checks in the whole ladder), then schema diffs where models moved layers. Record the outcome in decisions/ — a diff nobody wrote up is a diff nobody looked at three months from now.

nodes.label: Recce diff between built states
nodes.rationale: Every prior stage was supposed to be behaviour-preserving; lineage says what could break, only a diff says what did. Recce compares two built states — the base target writes the same DuckDB file under a base schema so both states are reachable from one connection and the seeds load once.

nodes.label: quality-stack skill
nodes.rationale: Every dbt project answers three questions with evidence, not vibes: did my change move the numbers (recce), does the data hold what the ontology asserts (dbt-expectations), what has been true over time (elementary). All three are pluggable tools: one tools.yaml decision per family, everything else derived — never hand-wire what bootstrap derives. Declaration is not proof: run the derivation chain and check each link.

nodes.label: Coverage is annotation
nodes.rationale: A mart with no generated expectations and no recce value checks is an unannotated mart — the fix is contracts/annotations.yaml, then re-derive: that one edit updates tests, review checks and monitors together. Judgements stay human: anomaly monitors and sharper expectations go in the model's own yml.

nodes.label: dignified-python skill
nodes.rationale: Production Python conventions adapted from dagster-io/skills dignified-python (Apache-2.0): 3.11-3.12 typing, LBYL over blanket except, pathlib everywhere, comment constraints the code cannot show, match the surrounding file's idiom rather than importing a house style.

nodes.label: Lazy-import heavy optional deps
nodes.rationale: dlt, dagster and dbt are imported inside functions rather than at module top so the platform core works without them installed.

nodes.label: Form first, colour last
nodes.rationale: Most bad charts are chosen the other way round, and no palette rescues the wrong form. The data's job picks the type; never a dual-axis chart — two measures of different scale become two charts, small multiples, or an index to a common base.

nodes.label: Theme-invariant mermaid styling
nodes.rationale: GitHub renders one mermaid source on both light and dark pages and does not recolour explicit classDef fills — so use pale fill + saturated stroke of the same hue + near-black ink. Escape every interpolated string (# opens an entity reference, quotes end the label, angle brackets are silently parsed as tags under htmlLabels). Never derive node ids from data: two boxes sharing an id are merged without error and a layer quietly vanishes.

nodes.label: Memory Note Module Scoping
