nodes.label: pf memory add
nodes.rationale: add writes the note into the right module and regenerates .memory/MEMORY.md; the index is never hand-edited because pf memory check fails the build when index and notes disagree.

nodes.label: Promotion Into CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: Promotion into an always-loaded, budgeted CLAUDE.md is a reviewed human step — that review is what makes the platform compound instead of accumulating notes nobody reads.

nodes.label: agent-context.yml PR Check Workflow
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: platform-tests.yml only runs on platform paths, so a PR adding a model and a note under groups/ never had its memory index, test index or repo map checked; agent-context.yml has no path filter and also checks the hand-written layer.

nodes.label: AGENT_CONTEXT_TOKEN Auto-Refresh Push
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: A push made with GITHUB_TOKEN never starts another workflow run, so a bot-fixed commit would sit on the PR with no checks and a required check would wait forever; the refresh job therefore needs a fine-grained PAT with contents: write.

nodes.label: pf tokens Advisory Step
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Advisory (continue-on-error) because the jaffle-shop card is 1585/1500 on main and fixing it is a person's decision; a hard step would redden every PR until that decision is made.

nodes.label: Execution Scope Over Vendor Role
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: The same model runs as a chat session, an Actions job and an inline completion, and each can do different things. Vendor roles (Claude = macro, Copilot = micro) broke the moment Copilot's coding agent got a shell and @claude in Actions lost its human.

nodes.label: detect_agent Environment Detection
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: detect_agent() in pf/memory.py knows PF_AGENT, CLAUDECODE, GEMINI_CLI and GITHUB_ACTIONS; a tool leaving no environment mark exports PF_AGENT instead.

nodes.label: Declined .agent-memory Ledger
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Declined twice: every field of a hand-off is already recorded (agent: on the note, git log, branch/PR, status:, the commit, a feedback note), the architecture is generated from kg/graph.json and CI-checked, and one mutable file every concurrent session appends to conflicts on every PR.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md Entry-Points Table
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: A new tool gets a row in the entry-points table; a per-vendor rules file is added only when the tool cannot read AGENTS.md.

nodes.label: Artifacts Also Saved Into docs/
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Artifacts are private to the owner's Claude account, so the claude.ai URL does not open signed out, on another account, or behind a network that blocks claude.ai. A file in docs/ opens from disk with no login, is reviewable in a PR, and is versioned with the code it describes.

nodes.label: pf tokens Budget Scope
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: pf tokens budgets only the cards, both CLAUDE.md levels, ROUTING.md and VENDOR-CARD.md, so a new docs/ file is not budgeted.

nodes.label: bot-findings Workflow
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: The repo's mechanism for never losing review comments when PRs merge; reinventing it with manual gh issue create would create fingerprint-less duplicates on the next nightly sweep.

nodes.label: (path, title) Issue Fingerprint
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Idempotency key stored as an HTML comment in the issue body; the review comment URL is cited there, so 'is this thread tracked?' is a search of issue bodies for the thread URL.

nodes.label: sweep Concurrency Group
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: All workflow_dispatch/schedule runs share the sweep group with cancel-in-progress: false, so dispatching several at once leaves one queued and cancels the rest — dispatch sequentially.

nodes.label: parse_review_body
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Added because the workflow read review threads only and skipped review bodies, missing 363 CodeRabbit 'Outside diff range' and 'Nitpick' findings across 137 PRs.

nodes.label: CR_RESET Explicit Section Resets
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Section resets must be an explicit list, not 'any unrecognised heading ends the section' — CodeRabbit phrases proposed-change summaries freely, and treating one as a boundary silently credited four files' findings to a fifth.

nodes.label: Epic #312 Sub-Issue Cap
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Epic #312 has hit GitHub's 100 sub-issue cap, so new findings fail to attach; it must be split before more findings land.

nodes.label: BOT_FINDINGS_DRY_RUN Verification
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: A dry run over every PR is the only thing that distinguishes 'parses more' from 'files duplicates'; without canonical_title, issue_path, locate and upsert adoption all four working, turning body parsing on duplicates 52 tracked issues.

nodes.label: Volatile Shared Checkout
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Several Claude CLI sessions work this one checkout at once; on 2026-09-20 one bulk-discarded tracked modifications across the whole tree (91 -> 43 dirty paths). Treat uncommitted work here as volatile and re-read files before claiming an edit landed.

nodes.label: Plumbing Commit Without Touching The Worktree
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: read-tree into a temp GIT_INDEX_FILE, hash-object, write-tree, commit-tree, git branch — never disturbs another session's dirty tree, but skips the pre-commit gate, so pf gate must be run by hand.
nodes.norm_label: plumbing commit without touching the worktree

nodes.label: land-195.sh PR Landing Script
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Implements scenarios S1-S18 for landing #196-#342: plan (read-only merge-tree simulation), issues, run FROM TO, one N, resume. Hand-merging what the script covers reintroduces the failures each scenario encodes.

nodes.label: S12 Duplicate Name/Key Check
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: A clean git merge can still be wrong: main and stack/09 each added a ducklake warehouse and git merged both into one dict where the later silently wins. S12 checks for duplicate top-level names and dict keys on every fold, and now reads package.json blocks too.

nodes.label: S13 TEST_GROUPS Map
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Guessing a test file's group from its imports was right for only 13 of 33 files, so the map is hand-decided and a file not in it stops for a human.

nodes.label: S14 CI Wait Before Merge
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: #318 merged while CI was red because the script accepted GitHub's unstable state; S14 waits for CI, stops on failures main does not share, and treats jobs that died at checkout as non-blocking.

nodes.label: S16 Rebuild What CI Checks
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Before a push, rebuild pf kg build then pf arch for every project the PR touches plus the repo-wide maps — and verify with pf kg check --strict, because pf kg build carries on when the dbt parse fails and rebuilds a graph recording no models at all.

nodes.label: S18 ruff Check Before Push
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: #340 cost three CI rounds for nine lint errors, one of them the script's own: S13's rehome() rewrites a file's only Path(__file__) and orphans the pathlib import. Only ruff's safe fixes are applied; the rest stop the run.

nodes.label: GitHub Native Stack Merge
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: gh pr merge is refused on members of a native stack ('must be merged using the asynchronous merge REST API'); only gh stack merge, sequentially, and base changes on native-stack PRs are refused.

nodes.label: pf report build Empty-Page Hazard
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Never run pf report build to 'resolve' a generated file: without transform/target/, collect_metrics finds nothing and it rewrites real pages as empty ones. Resolve a generated artefact by taking the side whose generator won, then confirm by calling the generator directly.

nodes.label: Missing asqav-compliance Upstream
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: The upstream of vendor/asqav-compliance no longer exists, so every CI job that checks out submodules dies at checkout; bumping or dropping that pin is a human decision.

nodes.label: Auto-Mode Classifier
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Independent of permissions.allow in .claude/settings.json — a Bash(gh stack merge:*) allow rule changes nothing. It judges a script by the merge code it contains, even in a read-only mode.

nodes.label: pf gate maxFiles 12 Commit Gate
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: The pre-commit hook runs pf gate --paths <staged>; gate.yaml maxFiles: 12 denies any larger commit. A conflicted merge always exceeds it and the classifier denies --no-verify, so resolved merges cannot be committed by the agent in auto mode — leave them staged for the user.

nodes.label: Denied Merge Actions
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Denied: merges into main, retargeting a stacked PR's base, bulk gh pr ready loops, --no-verify commits, sed on platform/ shared resources, and read-only probes issued after a first merge denial.

nodes.label: Allowed Prep Actions
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Allowed: merges into feature branches, one gh pr ready per call, pushes to feature branches, authored commits of <=12 files that pass the gate, PR/issue comments, workflow dispatch, worktree merges, and tests in a worktree.

nodes.label: ROUTER_BUDGET 700
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: The repo root CLAUDE.md is ROUTER_BUDGET = 700 in platform/src/pf/kg/card.py, loaded by every session. The committed version measured 698/700 — two tokens of headroom by design, not by accident. PROJECT_CLAUDE_BUDGET is 600 and GROUP_CLAUDE_BUDGET 400.

nodes.label: estimate_tokens Heuristic
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: len(text) // 4 in the same file, so ~2800 characters is the real ceiling for the 700-token router budget.

nodes.label: pf tokens CI Gate
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: Expanding the root CLAUDE.md from 50 to 174 lines measured 2109/700 and turned pf tokens from OK into a hard CI failure; anything beyond a one-line pointer belongs in a docs/*.md page, which carries no budget.

nodes.label: uv Workspace Hook Deadlock
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: The PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks run as uv run --project $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; with the workspace glob groups/*/projects/* unresolvable, every hook errors and every mutating tool is blocked — including Write, so the session cannot repair itself. Subagents and worktrees hit the same hook.

nodes.label: commodity-india Placeholder pyproject
nodes.author: claude-code
nodes.rationale: An untracked placeholder pyproject.toml keeps the uv workspace resolvable on branches where the real file is not tracked; never git add it, and remove it before checking out commodity-stack/*.

nodes.label: Generated Capability Policy Overlay
nodes.rationale: Generated from Capability.policies by pf bootstrap and pf new-project, layered over policy.yaml at load time by pf.ontology.model.load_ontology through the merge_policies guard: a capability may tighten the floor and may never relax it.

nodes.label: money-amount-bounded
nodes.rationale: A monetary column with no lower bound accepts the negative row a refund, a sign flip or a bad join produces, and it reaches a metric as a quietly smaller number.

nodes.label: source-declares-freshness
nodes.rationale: A mart is stale because its source was; monitoring the mart names the wrong artefact to go fix, and monitoring nothing means the first report of a stopped pipeline comes from whoever opened the dashboard.

nodes.label: anomaly-tests-do-not-gate-merge
nodes.rationale: An anomaly test judges data; a merge gate judges code. Wiring a statistical test into the gate blocks a correct change because yesterday's load was small, and the cure is always to weaken the test — which is how the monitoring stops working.

nodes.label: entity-isolation-enforced
nodes.rationale: A session that can read a sister project will carry an assumption across — a grain, a status enum, a revenue definition — and the resulting bug is invisible, because the code it came from is correct in the project it came from.

nodes.label: vendor-is-read-only
nodes.rationale: Editing a vendored upstream turns it into a fork wearing a submodule's name, and every later diff against upstream reads as drift nobody introduced.

nodes.label: agent-settings-schema-valid
nodes.rationale: A settings file the client rejects loads none of the plugins it declares and says so nowhere a session can see, silently removing kg_search and impact_analysis — and an agent with no graph reads files instead and never reports why.

nodes.label: Intent -> Constraint -> Artifact -> Evidence Chain
nodes.rationale: Modelled on OpenTopology. The platform already had rules but they lived in three disconnected places — prose in a skill, an if-statement in validate.py, a dbt test — so 'is this policy actually enforced?' had no answer. Every policy names the artifact that enforces it and the evidence that proves it ran; unenforced policies are the interesting output of pf policy status.

nodes.label: money-requires-currency
nodes.rationale: A monetary amount without its currency is not a number, it is a bug waiting for a second entity to be onboarded.

nodes.label: entity-requires-identity
nodes.rationale: A class with no identity property cannot participate in a derived join, so every BI and MDL projection of it is a guess.

nodes.label: link-must-be-in-topology
nodes.rationale: A foreign key pointing at a class the topology does not relate to is an undeclared join; undeclared joins are how two teams compute different revenue from the same warehouse.

nodes.label: pii-not-in-consumption
nodes.rationale: PII may land in raw and staging; it must not reach a mart or an exposure without a masking policy or an explicit, recorded waiver.

nodes.label: mart-declares-grain
nodes.rationale: Grain is the one fact a downstream consumer cannot infer and cannot survive guessing; an undeclared grain is how a join silently fans out.

nodes.label: metric-owns-aggregation
nodes.rationale: Aggregation policy belongs to exactly one metric definition; a mart column named revenue is a second definition that will drift from the first.

nodes.label: change-declares-blast-radius
nodes.rationale: A model or column change must report what it breaks before it lands, including the human who owns each affected exposure.

nodes.label: change-verified-against-baseline
nodes.rationale: A blast radius is a prediction made from lineage, and lineage cannot say whether the numbers moved; without a diff against a built baseline, 'safe' means 'nothing downstream references it', not 'nothing downstream changed'.

nodes.label: review-artifacts-exclude-pii
nodes.rationale: A value-level diff writes the rows it compared into the review tool's durable, shared state file, so diffing a PII column persists real addresses into an artefact that gets committed and passed around.

nodes.label: builds-record-observability
nodes.rationale: A dbt build that leaves no queryable record cannot be triaged; recording run and test results with history makes 'is this new, recurring, or flaky?' a query rather than an archaeology dig.

nodes.label: quality-floor-derived-from-ontology
nodes.rationale: Hand-written test coverage decays to whichever models someone remembered; deriving the floor from ontology roles makes coverage a function of annotation, and a wrong test a wrong role rather than a stale file.

nodes.label: secrets-never-in-context
nodes.rationale: A credential placed in a prompt, a model file or a committed artefact is durably persisted and replayed into every later session.

nodes.label: agent-authority-is-least-privilege
nodes.rationale: Least privilege that lives in a prompt is a request; in a denylist it is a control.

nodes.label: tool-contribution-may-only-tighten
nodes.rationale: A plugin system that can widen the policy judging it is not a policy; Tool.gate_sections() rejects a loosening contribution at construction, so an unsafe tool fails at import rather than silently permitting more.

nodes.label: agent-decisions-are-recorded
nodes.rationale: 'No rule applied' and 'a rule allowed it' are different facts, and only a record carrying both can answer what an agent was permitted to do — so allows are recorded as well as denies.

nodes.label: evidence-chain-is-tamper-evident
nodes.rationale: A log an agent can edit is not evidence; each record carries the hash of the one before and the head is anchored to a timestamp authority with no stake in what it says.

nodes.label: sister-projects-are-isolated
nodes.rationale: Business logic does not transfer between entities, so an assumption carried from one sister company into another is a bug by construction.

nodes.label: agent-authority-is-revocable
nodes.rationale: A control that cannot be switched off mid-incident is a control you find out about afterwards; revocation is checked before intent is written and an unreadable revocation file fails closed.

nodes.label: high-impact-actions-need-a-human
nodes.rationale: Human oversight is a chain that shows the approval, not a document that asserts it; an actor approving their own action is a finding rather than an approval.

nodes.label: model-routing-is-declared
nodes.rationale: Which model answers which step is a declared table, not whatever the caller passed; an unregistered step is recorded as such.

nodes.label: upstream-licences-are-reviewed
nodes.rationale: A licence constraint should be a fact in the registry rather than something someone once checked.

nodes.label: dev-serving-wire-is-read-only
nodes.rationale: The server holds the database read-only so the engine refuses writes at the catalog — not a parser, not a callback, nothing that can be argued with — and the client refuses non-read statements before the network hop using DuckDB's own parser.

nodes.label: dev-server-binds-localhost-only
nodes.rationale: A development database served on a routable interface is an exfiltration endpoint with a bearer token; the host is not a parameter of the serving path, so a routable dev server cannot be configured into existence, only programmed.

nodes.label: quack-token-never-leaves-the-machine
nodes.rationale: The serving token is a bearer credential: generated fresh per server, kept in a 0600 gitignored state file, denied to agent edits, and redacted from CLI output because a token echoed into a terminal outlives the server in scrollback and transcripts.

nodes.label: warehouse-custody-is-recorded
nodes.rationale: Serving, stopping and borrowing are the moments the dev database changes hands; each is a full chained ledger action, so 'who held the warehouse when' is a query over records.

nodes.label: control-baseline-is-declared
nodes.rationale: A risk register naming controls nobody enforces is a document; each entity declares in air.yaml which controls it commits to, derived on every run and blocking the merge when they fail. Deliberately carries no controls: entry — mapping it to a risk rather than a mitigation would be the category error the catalogue exists to stop.

nodes.label: Evidence Kinds Registry
nodes.rationale: Evidence kinds the chain may reference, each marked durable or not; an evidence entry naming something not listed here is itself a finding — that is how the chain stays honest.

nodes.label: Tool Precedence Order
nodes.rationale: Four upstream skill sets overlap here; without this order an agent answers a governed metric question with ad-hoc SQL. Raw SQL that recomputes a defined metric is a bug, not a shortcut.

nodes.label: Structure And Lineage Questions First
nodes.rationale: 'Where does X come from', 'what uses Y', 'what breaks if I change Z' go to kg_search, kg_neighbors, kg_path and impact_analysis. Never grep the repo first.

nodes.label: Governed Metric Before Ad-Hoc SQL
nodes.rationale: A business quantity goes to query_metrics; if no metric fits, say which definition is missing rather than silently falling back to SQL.

nodes.label: Cross-Sister Only Via _rollup
nodes.rationale: Cross-sister questions go through the _rollup project only, via ATTACH READ_ONLY; never read a sister project's files.

nodes.label: Data-Returning Tool Truncation Policy
nodes.rationale: Every data-returning tool is truncated by policy (schema + <=20 rows + counts); needing more means aggregating in SQL, not raising the limit.

nodes.label: Toolkit Inventory
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf context build from each toolkit's CONTEXT.md and each skill's frontmatter; precedence between toolkits lives in ROUTING.md.

nodes.label: dbt-expectations Toolkit
nodes.rationale: Distribution, range, type and row-count tests; static assertions are expectations, historical ones are dbt-elementary.

nodes.label: dlt-ingest Toolkit
nodes.rationale: For data that does not exist in the warehouse yet; annotate a source with ontology roles before writing any dbt model against it, and a load that left a table empty is red, not done.

nodes.label: dbt-elementary Toolkit
nodes.rationale: Anomaly detection and test-result triage; anomaly tests are warn, freshness belongs on the source, and these never gate a merge.

nodes.label: duckdb-ops Toolkit
nodes.rationale: Exploratory work only, subordinate to the metrics layer, read-only and truncated by policy.

nodes.label: dbt-govern Toolkit
nodes.rationale: Contracts, access modifiers and run troubleshooting; classify a failure before fixing it — upstream_data, model_logic, stale_source or test_too_strict.

nodes.label: dbt-semantic Toolkit
nodes.rationale: The mart declares the grain; the metric declares the aggregation policy. Never answer a metric question with ad-hoc SQL.

nodes.label: viz-standards Toolkit
nodes.rationale: Pick the form first and the colour last; status colours are reserved, and colourblind safety is computable so it is computed.

nodes.label: Copilot Scope Mapping
nodes.rationale: The rules are written once for every agent in AGENTS.md; this file exists only because Copilot cannot read AGENTS.md by default, and says where the rules are and which execution scope you are in.

nodes.label: Generated Memory Index
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf memory index; pf memory check fails the build when the index and the notes disagree, and the notes win — so a note cannot land without its line here and this file cannot claim a note that no longer exists.

nodes.label: Module Scope Of A Lesson
nodes.rationale: Root and platform/ apply everywhere; a group's notes apply to its sisters; a project's notes apply to it alone and are never read from a sister.

nodes.label: pf memory check
nodes.rationale: Runs in platform-tests.yml and in the suite; it is what keeps the index honest.

nodes.label: Unioned Bloom Graph Export
nodes.rationale: Eight project knowledge graphs unioned into 13,376 nodes and 14,399 relationships for Neo4j Bloom. Generated by pf bloom build and never hand-edited. CSV + Cypher rather than a dump, because a dump is unreviewable in a PR and needs that exact Neo4j version.

nodes.label: Qualified Node Ids
nodes.rationale: Model:orders exists in acme-us and acme-eu and they are different models; merging on the bare id would weld two sisters' lineage together — exactly what the isolation rule exists to prevent. Ids are group/project#local_id with the original kept as local_id.

nodes.label: Colour Is The Plane
nodes.rationale: Teal for physical and analytical, violet for semantic, slate for governance — the same three planes the KG Atlas uses; shade within a plane tracks containment. Without the perspective, Bloom renders grey circles and 13,376 of them is noise.

nodes.label: Column Hidden By Default
nodes.rationale: Column is 10,444 of 13,376 nodes (78%) and any view containing it is unreadable; one click brings it back.

nodes.label: Upstream To Downstream Edge Direction
nodes.rationale: Direction is a contract: every edge runs upstream -> downstream, so following one forwards always answers 'what depends on this'. feeds is named for that direction.

nodes.label: neo4j-graph-examples/bloom
nodes.rationale: The upstream reference this loader and perspective are modelled on, with three deliberate departures: CSV+Cypher over a dump, qualified ids, and flattened JSON properties.

nodes.label: floci S3 Emulator Service
nodes.rationale: pf.artifacts talks to an S3-compatible bucket and every other engine degrades to something on disk, so push/pull/ls and the recce baseline path could only be exercised against real object storage with real spend — and therefore mostly were not. Floci is an S3 on 4566 needing no account, replacing LocalStack Community after its March 2026 sunset.

nodes.label: Loopback-Only Port Binding
nodes.rationale: An unauthenticated object store that accepts any credential pair must not be reachable from the network, and the default bind would have made it so.

nodes.label: Opt-In Per Shell, Not Per Stack
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not wired into compose.yaml's stack service: pointing the control plane at it would mean the catalogue and recce publish artefacts into an in-memory emulator that forgets them on restart, and the first sign would be an empty review. A green floci run is a passing unit test, not a deployment check.
nodes.norm_label: opt-in per shell, not per stack

nodes.label: Explicit Region Pinning
nodes.rationale: FLOCI_DEFAULT_REGION is spelled out rather than defaulted because PF_ARTIFACTS_REGION on the client side has to match it, and a silent default on one side of the pair is how they drift apart; SigV4 signs the region, so a mismatch is a signature error that reads like a bad credential.

nodes.label: Three Cloud Root Modules
nodes.rationale: AWS, GCP and Azure each stand up the same five things — container runtime, Postgres, search, object store, secrets. The bolded differences (OpenSearch vs Elasticsearch, GCS XML+HMAC, per-key secrets) are where the clouds genuinely differ; everything else is the same design in three dialects.

nodes.label: Never Applied Verification Status
nodes.rationale: tofu validate and fmt pass on all three; plan and apply have never been run. Validation proves resource types and argument names are real — not that quotas exist, an image pulls, a SKU is available, the IAM suffices, or OpenMetadata comes up against a managed Postgres.

nodes.label: Repository Inside The Image At repo_path
nodes.rationale: Dagster's workspace.yaml holds absolute working_directory entries and there is no host path in Fargate, Cloud Run or Container Apps, so the repo must be in the image at a fixed path matching var.repo_path. This is the single most likely cause of a deployment that starts cleanly and orchestrates nothing.
nodes.norm_label: repository inside the image at repo_path

nodes.label: One Replica Per Module
nodes.rationale: Two replicas are two Dagster daemons sharing one run-storage schema, racing to launch the same schedules; scaling the control plane is a decomposition project, not a replica count.

nodes.label: OpenMetadata Migration Handling
nodes.rationale: Migrations are slow on a cold database: AWS uses a 600s health-check grace period, Azure a 60x10s startup probe, and GCP a separate Cloud Run job running the entrypoint's --migrate-only mode because its startup-probe budget does not stretch. Getting it wrong looks like a crash loop, which looks like a broken image.

nodes.label: PF_ARTIFACTS_REGION SigV4 Signing
nodes.rationale: SigV4 signs the region into every request. R2 requires the literal auto; real S3 rejects it with AuthorizationHeaderMalformed, which reads exactly like a bad credential.

nodes.label: GCS HMAC Key Pair
nodes.rationale: pf.artifacts speaks S3 and GCS answers S3 only on its XML API, which authenticates with HMAC keys — every other GCP integration wants the JSON key and the JSON key does not work here.

nodes.label: Exposure Is Opt-In
nodes.rationale: The control plane serves OpenMetadata, Dagster and every project's recce review with no authentication in front of any of it, and Dagster's UI can launch runs — so ingress_cidrs has no default, GCP defaults to an internal load balancer, and Azure's external ingress defaults to false. Opening any of them is a decision, not a step.

nodes.label: add-expectations Skill
nodes.rationale: dbt_expectations is the Great Expectations vocabulary as dbt tests; reach for it when the assertion is about a value's shape, which the built-in four cannot express.

nodes.label: Generate The Expectation From The Role
nodes.rationale: Annotations already declare intent, so the role determines the expectation — money_amount gets a >=0 range, event_time a current_timestamp bound that catches the year-2107 row, status_enum a built-in accepted_values rather than an expectation.
nodes.norm_label: generate the expectation from the role

nodes.label: Do Not Restate A Built-In Test
nodes.rationale: unique, not_null, accepted_values and relationships ship with dbt and read better in a diff; an expectation duplicating one is a second thing to update when the assumption changes.
nodes.norm_label: do not restate a built-in test

nodes.label: Error For Metric-Corrupting, Warn For Drift
nodes.rationale: error for anything that would corrupt a metric — a negative money_amount, a null key; warn for distribution drift, which is a question, not a defect.
nodes.norm_label: error for metric-corrupting, warn for drift

nodes.label: One Assumption Per Test
nodes.rationale: A test asserting a range and a type fails without saying which half broke. Thresholds go in dbt_project.yml vars, not literals in three models.

nodes.label: choose-a-test Skill
nodes.rationale: Five ways to assert something, chosen by what the assumption is about; picking the wrong one is how a suite grows without getting safer.

nodes.label: Cheapest Test That Expresses The Assumption
nodes.rationale: A built-in reads better in a diff than an expectation; an expectation is cheaper to reason about than a unit test; a unit test is deterministic where an anomaly test is statistical.
nodes.norm_label: cheapest test that expresses the assumption

nodes.label: Static vs Historical Assertion
nodes.rationale: 'Revenue is never negative' is static — an expectation. 'Revenue did not drop 60% overnight' is historical — Elementary. Writing the second as a hardcoded threshold produces a test that is wrong within a quarter and gets silenced rather than fixed.

nodes.label: Data vs Logic Test
nodes.rationale: A test that fails when the data changes is a data test; one that fails when the SQL changes is a unit test. Loading real rows to prove a CASE ladder works means you wanted a unit test.

nodes.label: Test vs Contract
nodes.rationale: 'This column is always a non-null integer' is a contract enforced at build; a test re-asserting a contracted column is checking the warehouse's own enforcement.

nodes.label: Run impact_analysis Before Adding A Test
nodes.rationale: It tells you how many things depend on the column you are about to assert — the honest measure of whether the test is worth its runtime, and which consumers to name if it ever fails.
nodes.norm_label: run impact_analysis before adding a test

nodes.label: debug-pipeline Skill
nodes.rationale: Diagnose a failed or empty dlt load with dlt Core's own tools — info, trace, failed-jobs, load-package, schema and the dataset API.

nodes.label: Pipeline Naming Convention
nodes.rationale: Pipelines are named <project>_<source> by pf.runtime.dlt_runtime.build_pipeline and keep their working folder under ~/.dlt/pipelines/<name>.

nodes.label: Read Row Counts Back
nodes.rationale: Staging reads exactly the pipeline's tables, so an empty one in dlt.attach(...).dataset().row_counts() is the whole story.

nodes.label: Classify Before Fixing A Load
nodes.rationale: Feed down, shape changed, contract too strict, or cursor wrong — never fix a red load by editing the raw table; fix the source or the contract, then pf seed.

nodes.label: drop Resource Rebackfill
nodes.rationale: dlt pipeline <name> drop <resource> removes its tables and state so the next run reloads it; deleting data/<project>.duckdb rebackfills everything because dlt drops local state when the dataset is gone.

nodes.label: Six Governance Planes
nodes.rationale: Five questions about agent behaviour, and no single mechanism answers more than one well. The planes are kept separate because they fail in different directions: a clean static scan with a broken chain means the controls exist and are not working; a clean chain with a failing scan means the instrumented paths are sound and something new is not. Neither result is the other's evidence.

nodes.label: Harness Permissions Plane
nodes.rationale: 7 deny, 4 ask, 13 allow in .claude/settings.json. Read denies keep secrets out of the context window entirely - a secret never read cannot be echoed into a log or a provider request body. The ask rules cover only outward-facing actions, encoding the shape of the whole model: an agent may write code freely and may not publish it. Weakest plane because it governs one client; first because it is cheapest, not strongest.

nodes.label: Path Gate (gate.yaml)
nodes.rationale: Evaluates paths one at a time plus one aggregate rule on the count, first hit wins. Bash is recorded but deliberately not path-gated because pretending a command string is a path would produce confident, wrong verdicts. maxFiles 12 is a reviewability control, not a safety one - it keeps an agent's unit of work inside what a person will actually read. Two files rather than one so installing a capability never rewrites gate.yaml, whose comments are where the reasons live.

nodes.label: TIGHTENING_SECTIONS Append-Only Merge
nodes.rationale: load_policy appends, never replaces, list-valued sections from gate.capabilities.yaml, and pf.tools.spec raises InvalidTool at import for a Tool contributing to denylist_except, autoMergeAllowlist, maxFiles or blockOn. That makes 'nothing installable can loosen the gate that judges it' structurally true rather than aspirational.

nodes.label: Ontology Policy Layer Plane
nodes.rationale: 26 policies governing claims about the platform rather than paths. 25 carry explicit controls: ids, which turns a compliance question into a traversal - pf air crosswalk eu-ai-act walks Article 12 to agent-decisions-are-recorded and from there to the chain and the anchor.

nodes.label: Provenance Ledger Plane
nodes.rationale: The only plane producing runtime evidence. Splitting intent from execution is what makes an ungated action detectable at all: a single line written after the fact cannot distinguish 'allowed and ran' from 'ran'. The hook writes INTENT before consulting the gate so a denial is recorded against an intent that already exists, and post_tool_use refuses to write a bare EXECUTION because that would manufacture an action that was never gated.

nodes.label: Canonical Record Form and the Float Ban
nodes.rationale: Keys sorted at every level, separators , and :, literal UTF-8, no floats anywhere, whole-second timestamps. 0.1 does not round-trip identically across languages, and a digest a second implementation cannot reproduce turns 'verifiable by anyone' into 'verifiable by us' without anything failing. prev sits inside the digest, which is what makes it a chain rather than a list with a pointer.
nodes.norm_label: canonical record form and the float ban

nodes.label: decision.not_enforced Finding
nodes.rationale: Catches the failure mode where the ledger looks strictest exactly where it is weakest - every blocked action recorded, and none of them blocked.

nodes.label: AIR Control Catalogue Plane
nodes.rationale: Catalogues are registered rather than hardcoded; ids are derived and never stored so an upstream type change renames a control and pf air verify catches it; absence is a state, not an error, so an uninitialised submodule assesses every control as unexercised. Coverage is derived on every run and never stored, because a recorded pass survives the change that invalidated it.

nodes.label: ASQAV Static Scan Plane
nodes.rationale: Reported, never enforced. The scanner is regex over source and reports Audit Trail GAP on a file whose every LLM call writes three hash-linked ledger records. Raising that score by renaming our functions to match its regexes would change the score and not the governance - a metric that can be satisfied by renaming is a metric that will be.

nodes.label: Earned Autonomy Ladder (L1/L2/L3)
nodes.rationale: A level is earned from a track record, not configured. Born level (LoopSpec.autonomy, changed in a PR) is kept apart from earned level (loop-levels.json, next to the ledger that proves it). The merge step is intentionally absent at every level: a human merges, a loop never does. Demotion is automatic and asymmetric because a reverted patch is the only hard evidence the loop's judgement was wrong in a way that reached a human.

nodes.label: Loop Circuit Breaker
nodes.rationale: Opens on three consecutive failures or a spent daily token budget and does not un-latch on its own: escalate to a human, clear by resolving the finding rather than by retrying.

nodes.label: Six Deliberately Separate Stores
nodes.rationale: The database is a mirror, not the record. chain.jsonl is the evidence and DuckDB is for querying; nothing writes to DuckDB on the hot path, and a mirror that disagrees with the chain loses. JSONL rather than a database so an auditor with sha256sum and python -c can check it.

nodes.label: Agent Threat Model
nodes.rationale: Names what is not caught as plainly as what is: chain-tail truncation (a valid prefix stays valid; an auditor holding an earlier anchored head is what catches it), anything outside the instrumented paths, attribution that is not authentication, a wrong-but-permitted action, the un-anchored window, prompt injection, and controls nobody thought to build.

nodes.label: F1 - Impact Warning Unreachable for Model SQL
nodes.rationale: autoMergeAllowlist is evaluated before impact_required and **/*.sql is on the allowlist, so changing a model's SQL - the highest-blast-radius edit in a data platform - is allowed silently while changing its schema.yml warns. Two of nine impact_required patterns are unreachable.
nodes.norm_label: f1 - impact warning unreachable for model sql

nodes.label: F2 - The Blocking Provenance Check Does Not Run in CI
nodes.rationale: The step is guarded by a test for provenance/chain.jsonl, which is gitignored, so a CI checkout never has a ledger and the step passes after printing 'No ledger in this checkout'. The audit runs where the evidence is, which is not CI.
nodes.norm_label: f2 - the blocking provenance check does not run in ci

nodes.label: F3 - The Two Verifiers Disagree by Construction
nodes.rationale: The bundled auditor checks only integrity and completeness but is stricter on thresholds, exiting 1 on any missing stage where the platform audit rates a dangling action a warn. An action in flight at export time fails the auditor's copy and passes ours.
nodes.norm_label: f3 - the two verifiers disagree by construction

nodes.label: F7 - One Agent Path Writes No Provenance
nodes.rationale: pf.agents.ask.answer_live runs a bounded tool-use loop directly against the client rather than through base.call, so its tokens are invisible to the loop budget and the circuit breaker.
nodes.norm_label: f7 - one agent path writes no provenance

nodes.label: Per-Project Architecture Map
nodes.rationale: About 2,000 tokens answering what an agent would otherwise answer by reading twenty directories. Committed and dateless by design: the context card stamps its generation date, so committing it would rewrite eight files daily and say nothing, while a dateless map makes pf arch --check measure drift rather than noise.

nodes.label: pf.architecture.FEATURES Registry
nodes.rationale: A registry rather than a template because a template is precisely how a project feature goes missing - catalog/ and evals/ were added to the scaffolder long after the first overview was written and appeared in none of them. Every feature is reported including the absent ones; detection is by path glob so a feature is detectable in a project that cannot import its own code and has no warehouse.

nodes.label: Unmapped Entry Detection
nodes.rationale: Any top-level entry no feature claims is listed and fails pf arch --check, so a directory added by a future capability shows up as a hole in the map rather than not showing up at all. Its first run reported tools.yaml, which nothing had ever documented.

nodes.label: viz.lint Diagram Linter
nodes.rationale: Checks the four mermaid defects that are invisible in source and expensive in the render - an edge to an undeclared node, two nodes sharing an id, an undefined class, a raw < in a label. A malformed diagram renders as a red box while the job that produced it exits 0, which is why this is a test and not an eyeball.

nodes.label: Architecture Map Token Budget
nodes.rationale: 4,000 tokens, measured at 2,000-2,200 across eight projects. When one goes over, cap a section rather than raise the budget: the map that grows with the project is the one that silently stops being cheaper than reading.

nodes.label: Shared platform/ Tier vs Per-Entity groups/
nodes.rationale:
platform/ is shared by every project and groups//projects/

/ is not. Business logic never transfers between entities - an assumption carried across is a bug - and gate.yaml's platform_denylist refuses the write in both directions.
nodes.community_name: Platform Docs — Commodity End To End
nodes.norm_label: shared platform/ tier vs per-entity groups/

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.rationale: Declarative: files, settings, gate rules, CI jobs, from one entry in pf.capabilities.CAPABILITIES. pf bootstrap --all carries a new one into projects that already exist and refuses a partial backfill - a capability applies only when every file it writes is absent - so it can never overwrite a file someone has edited.

nodes.label: Tool (pf.tools entry point)
nodes.rationale: A capability that also runs - Dagster assets, a UI, CLI verbs - registered through a pf.tools entry point in any installed package. Adding one touches no scaffolder, no CLI and no workflow.

nodes.label: Three Context Cost Tiers
nodes.rationale: Always-on and budgeted, on demand, and queried-never-loaded. pf tokens fails the build when an always-on artefact exceeds its budget because that tier is paid by every request for the life of the project. The graph is the opposite: never loaded, only asked.

nodes.label: Merge Gate Path
nodes.rationale: Edit to pre-commit to gate rules to blast radius to the per-project workflow, with platform-tests.yml running alongside. pf arch check runs inside that workflow and the suite, so a change that alters the shape of the repository cannot merge while the document still describes the old one.

nodes.label: One Project, Source to Consumer
nodes.rationale: external source to dlt resource to raw DuckDB schema to staging to marts to the semantic layer to exposures, with annotations, marts and semantic models feeding the knowledge graph. The names are platform conventions, not one company's data.
nodes.community_name: Platform Docs — Commodity End To End

nodes.label: The Artefact Store
nodes.rationale: Build output git should not carry, in an S3-compatible bucket. Committed recce baselines held for seven projects at ~1.4MB each but not for jaffle-shop, whose 996 marts make the same three files 30MB - larger than the whole repository history - rewritten with fresh timestamps on every review run. Ignoring them alone would have been the other half of the bad trade, since CI and the control plane both read them.

nodes.label: Repository-Mirroring Key Layout
nodes.rationale: Keys mirror the repository so the bucket reads like a checkout, with a trailing ref segment - what git gave for free and object storage does not. A baseline is keyed by the ref it was built from and shared; keying it per developer would give every branch a baseline captured from its own code, and a diff against yourself reports clean. A review is keyed by the branch under review so two branches write two keys rather than racing for one.

nodes.label: floci Local Object Store
nodes.rationale: pf artifacts was the one subsystem with no local mode - every other engine degrades to something on disk, but a bucket is a bucket. floci proves the shape (key layout, absence handled as absence, push/pull round-tripping) and nothing about a real bucket being reachable. Treat a green run as a passing unit test, not a deployment check.

nodes.label: Publishing Never Changes a Verdict
nodes.rationale: Every upload is wrapped: a failed push warns and the command keeps its exit code. A captured baseline that did not upload is still a captured baseline, and a network blip should not read as a failed build. Equally, a local baseline wins - re-pulling would silently replace a capture made deliberately.

nodes.label: Known Gap - Baseline Staleness
nodes.rationale: A baseline is only a baseline while it matches the branch it claims to be from. Pulled by every PR and refreshed by nobody, it drifts one commit further from main on each merge, and the diffs stay green because the comparison state no longer exists rather than because nothing moved. Not a regression from the store - committed baselines went stale on the same cadence.

nodes.label: pf artifacts migrate - Push, Verify, Untrack
nodes.rationale: The order is the whole safety of the command: untracking first would, on a failed upload, leave the artefacts nowhere - still in git history and recoverable, but 'recoverable from history' is not a state to leave a merge gate in.
nodes.norm_label: pf artifacts migrate - push, verify, untrack

nodes.label: power-tools Session Layer
nodes.rationale: Commands, read-only agents, hooks and the pf MCP server in one toolkit. pf loop audit scores it, including two checks that exist because this exact configuration silently broke once: plugin marketplace resolves, and MCP tools available to projects.

nodes.label: Memory Layering (always-on, on-demand, queried, remembered)
nodes.rationale: The widely-circulated advice is 'put everything in CLAUDE.md'; here the repo enforces the opposite, because always-on context is paid by every request for the life of the project. Module .memory/notes/ live in the repo rather than ~/.claude so every other agent reading AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md or the Copilot instructions sees the same notes.

nodes.label: The pf MCP Server
nodes.rationale: 23 tools scoped to one project by PF_PROJECT_DIR. Every data-returning tool truncates - schema, at most 20 rows, summary stats, never a raw dump - and that policy lives in the server rather than in an instruction anyone can forget. In a root session warehouse and graph tools answer 'not inside a project', which is the isolation working.

nodes.label: Read-Only Verification Subagents
nodes.rationale: All four declare disallowedTools Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit. A verifier that can edit stops being a second opinion and becomes a second author.

nodes.label: The Formatter Never Removes Code
nodes.rationale: Autofix is restricted to import sorting. A bare ruff check --fix-only deletes unused imports, and an import added moments before the code that uses it is legitimately unused - a hook that removes what the agent is about to use is worse than no hook. SQL that will not parse is skipped rather than half-formatted.

nodes.label: pf workflow link
nodes.rationale: Replaces two harness directories with symlinks to logs/workflows/ so runs are written inside the repo as they happen - nothing copied, nothing moved, which is why progress is visible mid-run. workflows/ itself is deliberately not linked, because Claude Code's cleanup sweep recurses with readdir and would delete run history a month later; today isDir uses lstat so a symlinked directory is skipped, but that is a safe accident, not a guarantee.

nodes.label: Corrections to the Power-User Guide
nodes.rationale: A list of widely-circulated flags, files and env vars that do not exist in Claude Code 2.1.x - .claude/permissions.json, --scope/--exclude, --max-context, claude auth login, mcp restart --all. Marketplace source paths resolve from the marketplace root, and getting that wrong silently loads zero plugins, which is what happened here.

nodes.label: Change the Generator, Not the File
nodes.rationale: A generated artefact is committed so it can be diffed in review, not so it can be edited; gate.yaml's denylist refuses the edit and denylist_except lets git carry it anyway. Hand-editing one is silently discarded by the next regeneration.
nodes.norm_label: change the generator, not the file

nodes.label: Verifying a Regenerated Artefact
nodes.rationale: A regenerated artefact is only safe to commit when the generator could see everything the committed copy was built from - this tree's generators degrade silently rather than failing. No warehouse deletes thousands of Column nodes; a stale dbt manifest makes every downstream read confidently wrong. Reproduce the job's own order and diff node sets rather than lines, because node order in graph.json is unstable and a 16-node addition can render as a 7,500-line diff.

nodes.label: The Commit Gate Before Staging
nodes.rationale: maxFiles 12, platform_denylist refusing a project session writing platform/**, and impact_required meaning the blast radius must be reported first. Deletions are not shown to the gate: pre_commit.sh selects --diff-filter=ACMR deliberately, so a delete-only commit passes every rule unexamined.

nodes.label: Known Gap - A Registry Entry With No Submodule
nodes.rationale: The vendor registry carries a full entry for floci but .gitmodules has never had a vendor/floci submodule. Adding it is a vendoring decision the router reserves for a human, so it is flagged rather than fixed.
nodes.norm_label: known gap - a registry entry with no submodule

nodes.label: Byte-Stable Cached Prefix for Loop Agents
nodes.rationale: pf.agents.base.cached_prefix builds a byte-stable system prefix from ROUTING.md, loop-constraints.md, the context card with its generation date stripped, and the group and project CLAUDE.md rules. Byte-stable matters because the prefix is what the provider caches - regenerating the card must not bust it - and the contract eval tier checks exactly that.
nodes.norm_label: byte-stable cached prefix for loop agents

nodes.label: The Layer Contract (dlt extracts, dbt transforms)
nodes.rationale: The line between them is the raw dataset and nothing crosses it in the wrong direction. Never transform inside a dlt resource, so the raw stage stays rebuildable from the feed alone; never join in staging, so pf gen-staging can run again without losing a hand edit that was never supposed to be there. Recorded in ADR-0004, whose reasoning is that the reference workbench's transformation path needs a proprietary package whose licence excludes Dagster.
nodes.community_name: Platform Docs — Commodity End To End
nodes.norm_label: the layer contract (dlt extracts, dbt transforms)

nodes.label: Five Provenance Stages
nodes.rationale: INTENT, DECISION, EXECUTION, CHAIN, TIMESTAMP. The order is the guarantee: an INTENT written after the fact is a story, and a DECISION written after the EXECUTION is a rationalisation. A log cannot answer whether this was what the agent meant to do, nor whether anything checked - a ledger holding only refusals proves the gate can say no but not that it was consulted.
nodes.community_name: Platform Docs — Commodity End To End

nodes.label: provenance/chain.jsonl
nodes.rationale: Append-only, machine-written runtime state, gitignored except the anchor tokens: every branch would conflict on it and a merge would silently reorder a hash chain into an invalid one. Durability comes from anchoring the head and archiving pf provenance export, not from git. It is on the gate's denylist because an agent that can edit the record of what it did has no record of what it did.

nodes.label: Two-Anchor Timestamping (RFC 3161 + OpenTimestamps)
nodes.rationale: Two anchors because they fail differently: RFC 3161 is immediate and legally recognised but its trust is the TSA's key, while OpenTimestamps needs no trusted party and stays verifiable as long as Bitcoin does but costs hours. Deliberately not in the hook - both need the network, and a PreToolUse hook that makes a network call adds its latency and failure modes to every tool call. Anchoring runs where the ledger is, and that is not CI.

nodes.label: pf provenance verify (the audit)
nodes.rationale: Four questions ordered by what they can prove - integrity, completeness, coverage, oversight - plus decision.not_enforced. The standalone verify_provenance.py is stdlib-only and imports nothing from the platform, and is shipped beside the chain so an auditor receives the evidence and the means to check it in one bundle.

nodes.label: Fail-Open by Default, Fail-Closed Where It Counts
nodes.rationale: A governance system whose failure mode is 'the whole team stops' gets switched off, and a switched-off system records nothing. Two things ignore the flag because a control a setting can bypass is not a control: revocation, and an unreadable revoked.json - 'I cannot tell whether you are revoked' must not resolve to 'carry on'.
nodes.community_name: Platform Docs — Commodity End To End
nodes.norm_label: fail-open by default, fail-closed where it counts

nodes.label: ASQAV as a Second Opinion
nodes.rationale: Carried because it fails in the opposite direction: runtime evidence says nothing about code no agent has exercised, and a static scan says nothing about whether any of it ran. Reported never enforced, and pinned as a submodule run from the checkout so the code that judges our compliance cannot change without a commit here.

nodes.label: The Fourth Side - A Published Control Catalogue
nodes.rationale: The five stages prove what an agent did and ASQAV asks whether controls exist in source; neither says which controls there should be, and for a regulated deployment that is the part somebody external judges. The controls: field is what lets the ledger answer a question it could not answer before.
nodes.norm_label: the fourth side - a published control catalogue

nodes.label: Three Planes, One Store
nodes.rationale: kg_nodes and kg_edges; the structure lives in the kind column and divides into physical/analytical, semantic and governance. Nothing is declared in NODE_KINDS or EDGE_KINDS that the builder does not emit, because a declared-but-unbuilt kind makes traversals that filter on it look implemented when they are dead. The four cross-plane edges are the point of the design.

nodes.label: Every Edge Runs Upstream to Downstream
nodes.rationale: A contract, not a convention: out_edges is always 'what depends on n' and in_edges 'what n was built from', with no per-kind exceptions to memorise. feeds is named for that direction; it was once derives_from, which pointed the other way and made every rendered lineage path read backwards. has_column is the single deliberate exception, walked upward and encoded in UPWARD_KINDS.
nodes.norm_label: every edge runs upstream to downstream

nodes.label: impact_analysis
nodes.rationale: Traverses five of the fourteen edge kinds. It is a lineage instrument, not a governance one: a change that breaks a governs or realises relationship comes back 'safe to change' because those edges were never walked. Severity is structural rather than a judgement call - any exposure or metric in the radius is breaking, models alone are review, nothing is safe.

nodes.label: kg_path
nodes.rationale: Undirected shortest path, max 8 hops. It renders chain order, not edge direction: every hop prints as an arrow regardless of which way the edge ran, so the chain is correct and the arrow is not lineage.

nodes.label: kg_search
nodes.rationale: Substring over name, label and id, case-insensitive, capped at 40 - the entry point when you have a word rather than a node id.

nodes.label: kg_neighbors
nodes.rationale: Undirected, walking both in and out edges. Narrow with kinds= before raising depth, and use it rather than impact_analysis for semantic or policy consequences, because it reads the plane directly.

nodes.label: The Ontology Is Resolved at Project Scope
nodes.rationale: build_graph calls load_project_ontology; both narrower choices were bugs one layer apart. Building from the platform ontology drops every class a steward approved into the group extension; building from the group ontology drops the project's policy overlay, so a project that raised a severity was governed by rules its own graph did not contain. Each Policy node carries a scope prop because severity alone cannot distinguish an obligation this project took on from one the platform carries.
nodes.norm_label: the ontology is resolved at project scope

nodes.label: Three Ways the Graph Is Thinner Than Reality
nodes.rationale: A missing dbt manifest is silent, so every blast radius returns empty - 'safe to change' for a change it could not see. Undocumented columns are backfilled from information_schema but never inferred as PII, so a backfilled column's pii false means not declared rather than not sensitive. Edges to nodes that were never built are dropped, so a missing input removes edges silently rather than leaving dangling ones.
nodes.norm_label: three ways the graph is thinner than reality

nodes.label: GateNotExercised
nodes.rationale: The gate raises rather than passing when the graph holds zero models, and a project with no manifest reports 'not exercised' rather than clean. A green tick meaning 'found nothing' is worse than no gate, because it is trusted.

nodes.label: pf kg check
nodes.rationale: Compares the tracked graph.json against the dbt manifests, and only what a runner without a warehouse can see - columns are backfilled from information_schema, so comparing those too would be red on every pull request forever, and a permanently red check is one nobody reads. Reaches every project because the job is contributed by a capability rather than written into a workflow file.

nodes.label: No Arguments Means Everything
nodes.rationale: build, card and check all widen the same way. A command that can only be pointed at one project at a time gets run for the project you remembered, which is how seven graphs end up a month stale while the eighth is fine.

nodes.label: What the Graph Will Never Tell You
nodes.rationale: Anything about a sister - graphs are per project and hold no cross-project edges, so cross-entity blast radius is assessed in the rollup project against its own graph and nowhere else. Business logic, which lives in project-confined dbt models. And freshness: the graph has no clock, so when an answer contradicts a file you can see, the graph is the stale one.
nodes.community_name: Platform Docs — Commodity End To End
nodes.norm_label: what the graph will never tell you

nodes.label: The Policy Layer
nodes.rationale: Vocabulary is shared and obligations are not. Two sisters must mean the same thing by Payment or a roll-up adds two numbers that merely share a name, but what must hold is genuinely local - acme-eu answers to GDPR and acme-us does not - so policy layers where the rest of the ontology deliberately does not.

nodes.label: Overlays May Only Tighten
nodes.rationale: A layer may add, tighten or enforce, and nothing else. A relaxation raises at load time rather than check time, because a relaxed policy that only failed when something tripped over it would be discovered by the incident it was written to prevent. A governance layer that each project can weaken is not a governance layer.

nodes.label: PolicyRelaxation
nodes.rationale: Subclasses ValueError and must be re-raised before validate._ontology_for's (OSError, ValueError) fallback, or a project that tried to weaken a policy would be validated against the very policy set it tried to weaken. A relaxation is a finding, not a fallback.

nodes.label: An Omitted severity Means Inherit
nodes.rationale: In a base document an omitted severity defaults to error, because a rule whose severity was forgotten should shout rather than whisper. In an overlay it must mean inherit, or an entry that only adds an enforced_by line would silently escalate the policy - a tightening nobody wrote and nobody would spot in the diff.

nodes.label: applies_to and params Are Not Overridable
nodes.rationale: Narrowing applies_to reads like a refinement and is really a partial delete: retargeting pii-not-in-consumption from pii_* to pii_email stops covering pii_name and pii_phone with nothing in the diff shaped like a removal. A project that needs different targeting declares a new policy with a new id, where the addition is visible as an addition.
nodes.norm_label: applies_to and params are not overridable

nodes.label: An Unenforced Policy Surfaces Honestly
nodes.rationale: A policy that names no enforced_by reports as unenforced rather than passing. An unenforced policy that reports pass is worse than no policy at all, because it ends the conversation.

nodes.label: SEVERITY_RANK
nodes.rationale: info 0, warning 1, error 2 - what makes tightening-only a computation rather than a convention.

nodes.label: The governance Capability
nodes.rationale: The overlay arrives as a capability rather than a hardcoded scaffold step, default_enabled because an opt-in capability reaches only the projects whose author remembered the flag. The seeded file is inert, with policies [] and every example commented out, because a capability that silently tightened the gate on adoption would be discovered as a broken build in a project nobody had touched.

nodes.label: Capability.preserve
nodes.rationale: Names files written when absent and left alone when present. apply() otherwise rewrites every target wholesale, which is correct for a generated artefact and destructive for one a human is expected to edit - and pf capability-add deliberately bypasses the all-or-nothing guard.

nodes.label: load_ontology Is Cached - Overlays Must Never Write Through It
nodes.rationale: An overlay that mutated the lru_cached platform ontology would leak one project's policy into every other, and the test that caught it would be somewhere else entirely. Every overlaying path returns a copy owning its own policy list.
nodes.norm_label: load_ontology is cached - overlays must never write through it

nodes.label: What Is Deliberately Not Layered
nodes.rationale: Concepts, topology and relations stay at platform and group scope. Project-scoped vocabulary would mean acme-rollup summing two things that merely share a name - the 'assumption carried across is a bug' failure moved out of the vocabulary, where pf check can catch it, and into the arithmetic, where nothing can.

nodes.label: Per-Project Atlas Page
nodes.rationale: The platform atlas shows facts identical in all eight projects; what it cannot show is one project - which node kinds it uses, what its lineage looks like, which policies it tightened locally, where it is thin. Not committed, because the page stamps the graph's build time and carrying it would rewrite eight files on every dbt build and say nothing.

nodes.label: The dbt Runtime Atlas Hook
nodes.rationale: Attached at pf.runtime.dbt_runtime.dbt(), the one function every dbt invocation goes through, which is what makes the hook reach every caller without any of them remembering to call it. It fires only for run and build, and a hook can never fail a build - _run_hooks swallows everything, because publishing a picture of the graph is a convenience and the run is the thing that matters.

nodes.label: Atlas Config Layering and Unknown-Key Refusal
nodes.rationale: Platform defaults, group, project - later winning key by key, so a group can set it once and a project can opt out without arguing with its siblings. An unknown key is refused by name rather than ignored: silently dropping 'enabeld' is how a typo becomes a setting nobody has.
nodes.norm_label: atlas config layering and unknown-key refusal

nodes.label: pf new-project --plan
nodes.rationale: Scaffolding is cheap to run and expensive to run wrong - bootstrap backfills what is missing but never removes what should not have been added. The plan resolves the whole scaffold and writes nothing, replacing ~8,000 tokens of exploration with ~124: exploration whose answers are short, fixed and knowable by the scaffolder is the whole category of thing that should never cost an agent a file read.

nodes.label: Scaffold Blockers vs Warnings
nodes.rationale: Two blockers, both mistakes that have actually been made: the group does not exist, and the directory is already taken. A missing credential only warns, because a production target is inert until DBT_TARGET=prod asks for it and every project is created on a machine that cannot reach its warehouse - blocking there would block the normal case.

nodes.label: pf.scaffold.bootstrap.STEPS
nodes.rationale: One ordered idempotent list shared by new-project and bootstrap. The steps used to be inlined in new-project, so every capability added later had to be hand-patched into existing projects and each one was a silent hole until somebody noticed.

nodes.label: Group or Project?
nodes.rationale: Put a new entity in an existing group only if a roll-up across it and its sisters would be arithmetically meaningful. Two companies that mean different things by Payment cannot be summed, and the roll-up is where that surfaces - as a number, silently. If the vocabulary does not transfer, it is a new group.
nodes.community_name: Platform Docs — Commodity End To End

nodes.label: Roll-Up Project
nodes.rationale: Names its sisters by alias and attaches each READ_ONLY, checking the conformed marts exist with one column set before anything reads them; a sister whose columns differ is refused by name.
nodes.community_name: Platform Docs — Commodity End To End

nodes.label: Read the Card, Not the Scaffolded Files
nodes.rationale: The scaffolder knows what it made; reading twenty-two generated files to rediscover it is the most expensive possible way to learn something you were just told.
nodes.norm_label: read the card, not the scaffolded files

nodes.label: The Four-Layer Semantic Stack
nodes.rationale: policy (what must hold), topology (how they relate), concepts (what things are), annotations (where they live). Built in this order deliberately: a topology without identity cannot generate a join, and a policy without an ontology has nothing to attach to. Only the bottom layer is per project, with policy the one exception that also layers.

nodes.label: Why Relations Are Nodes, Not Edges
nodes.rationale: A bare edge cannot carry a name, an inverse, or a binding. MDL requires relationships[].name, a reverse-reading agent needs inverse, and the physical join must be bound to an actual foreign-key column.
nodes.norm_label: why relations are nodes, not edges

nodes.label: Deriving a Join Condition
nodes.rationale: Nothing is guessed from a naming convention: the column realises a named relation, the relation's range carries the identity, and cardinality is inverted when the foreign key sits on the range side because the FK is always on the many side.

nodes.label: Projections of the Graph
nodes.rationale: MDL, OWL, the context card and the impact report are all projections, never a parallel hand-maintained file.

nodes.label: Vendored Upstreams Index
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf vendor card from the registry; the reverse lookup is pf vendor why <file>.

nodes.label: Contracts That Can Fail a Build
nodes.rationale: Our output is validated against the vendored file, not against memory, so an upstream field becoming required breaks the build at the pin bump instead of during a live ingestion.
nodes.norm_label: contracts that can fail a build

nodes.label: The Vendor Registry (path-pair adoptions)
nodes.rationale: Every borrowing is a path pair - one file upstream, one or more of ours - so the claim is verifiable rather than remembered. 24 upstreams, 88 adoptions, 51 explicit declines; the declines are recorded because a decision not to take something is as load-bearing as taking it.

nodes.label: vendor.lock.json Is Not the Gitlink
nodes.rationale: The submodule pointer records which commit is checked out; the lock records which commit a person reviewed, plus a git OID per adopted path. They diverge the moment someone runs --remote without reading anything, and the gap between them is the only thing that makes drift observable. Automation opens a PR and never approves, because approval means a human read the diff and a workflow cannot mean that.

nodes.label: WrenAI MDL Schema
nodes.rationale: Field names and the cardinality enum come from the vendored schema, not from memory - layoutVersion being an integer was got wrong once by guessing, which is the reason the schema is vendored at all.

nodes.label: Three Tiers and One Prohibition
nodes.rationale: Platform, group, project - and the prohibition that a project may never read another project. Containment is the permission model: inner tiers read outward, never sideways.
nodes.community_name: Platform Docs — Commodity End To End

nodes.label: One Price, From the API to the Board
nodes.rationale: The real chain in commodity-us, with the rule that governs each hop written between the stages: dlt lands raw only, annotations drive everything downstream, staging is generated and cleans only, minor units then units then FX, the conformed core is identical in every sister, and only the market marts carry the market's own law.
nodes.community_name: Platform Docs — Commodity End To End
nodes.norm_label: one price, from the api to the board

nodes.label: The One Sister Allowed to Look Sideways
nodes.rationale: A cross-market question cannot be answered inside a market, and the answer is not to relax the rule but a fourth kind of thing: a roll-up that reaches its sisters through a read-only attachment to their warehouse files rather than by reading their code. Its refusal of a sister whose conformed models differ is the load-bearing part - a comparison is only meaningful if every market computed its landed price the same way, so the roll-up is also the test.
nodes.community_name: Platform Docs — Commodity End To End
nodes.norm_label: the one sister allowed to look sideways

nodes.label: Five Rules That Outrank Any Request
nodes.rationale: The knowledge a schema cannot hold, written where an agent reads it before starting: a price is not additive, convert in order, a sister is a market, the conformed core is identical everywhere, and extraction never transforms.
nodes.community_name: Platform Docs — Commodity End To End
nodes.norm_label: five rules that outrank any request

nodes.label: Convert in Order
nodes.rationale: Minor-unit quotes first, then units of measure, then foreign exchange. Any other order is quietly wrong.
nodes.community_name: Platform Docs — Commodity End To End

nodes.label: A Price Is Not Additive
nodes.rationale: It is a unit price, never a money amount. A mean is a sum divided by a count within one commodity, never across commodities or markets.
nodes.community_name: Platform Docs — Commodity End To End

nodes.label: The Graph Is Asked, Not Read
nodes.rationale: Which is why a session can reason about a warehouse it has never opened; and the generated artefacts are committed on purpose, so a pull request shows the change and its consequences together.
nodes.norm_label: the graph is asked, not read

nodes.label: Published Knowledge Graph Atlas Page
nodes.rationale: The rendered platform atlas: a card says what is here, an atlas says what a graph is.

nodes.label: Merging Is a Narrowing, Not a Trigger
nodes.rationale: Every workflow fires on pull_request and only two also declare push to main, so only two survive the merge. Deliberate - the per-project checks judge a diff against its base and a merge commit has no base to judge against - but the consequence is that the path gate, the project checks and the platform suite are not re-run at merge.
nodes.norm_label: merging is a narrowing, not a trigger

nodes.label: The Three Post-Merge Governance Jobs
nodes.rationale: Designed to fail in different directions - runtime evidence, static analysis, an external control catalogue - but on the last real merge two of the three failed in the same direction: a dead vendor submodule taking down the recursive checkout before either reached its first line of code.

nodes.label: A Fast Queue Cancels Its Own Audit Trail
nodes.rationale: The concurrency group keys on github.ref, which is unique per branch on a pull request and constant on main - so every merge cancels the still-running governance check of the merge before it. The faster the team ships, the less of it runs.
nodes.norm_label: a fast queue cancels its own audit trail

nodes.label: The changes Job Routes Governance by Diff
nodes.rationale: Each project workflow turns the diff into five booleans and conditions every downstream job on one, so governance scales with what was touched rather than running everywhere every time. This is the reassuring half - the governance that works happens before the merge.
nodes.norm_label: the changes job routes governance by diff

nodes.label: M1 - The Post-Merge Governance Check Has Never Passed
nodes.rationale: 47 runs, 30 failed, 17 cancelled, 0 succeeded. A permanently red required-looking check is worse than no check: it trains everyone to ignore the one signal that is supposed to mean something. The fix needs an owner, not an agent, because bumping a pin is a human decision.
nodes.norm_label: m1 - the post-merge governance check has never passed

nodes.label: M3 - The Ledger Audit Runs Where the Evidence Isn't
nodes.rationale: The docs call pf provenance verify the blocking check in CI, but the ledger is gitignored runtime state so a checkout never has one and the step always skips. The reasoning is sound; the effect is that the audit never runs anywhere CI can see.
nodes.norm_label: m3 - the ledger audit runs where the evidence isn't

nodes.label: M4 - One Project Is Missing Three Governance Jobs
nodes.rationale: commodity-india has no air-baseline, kg-current or architecture job. The workflows are generated from each project's capabilities, so this is a capability gap showing through - but nothing in CI compares one project's job list to its siblings', so it stays invisible. The newest entity in the fleet is the least governed.
nodes.norm_label: m4 - one project is missing three governance jobs

nodes.label: M5 - A Green Tick That Means 'Nothing to Check'
nodes.rationale: The provenance job reports success having verified no ledger - honest in its log and misleading on the checks list. 'Passed' and 'had nothing to look at' should not be the same tick.
nodes.norm_label: m5 - a green tick that means 'nothing to check'

nodes.label: Generated Suite Index
nodes.rationale: Generated by pf test index from the suite's own docstrings; reading it costs ~800 tokens against ~4,000 lines of test code and it cannot drift, because pf test check fails when it and the suite disagree and gate/test_suite_index.py runs that check inside the suite itself.

nodes.label: tests/gate - What Blocks a Merge
nodes.rationale: 16 files, 255 tests covering the path gate, provenance, AIR, evals, loops, memory index, diagrams and the suite's own index.

nodes.label: tests/graph - The Graph and the Always-On Context Tier
nodes.rationale: 8 files, 149 tests over the architecture map, the per-project atlas, the context card, the Evidence projection, MDL relationships, graph currency and ADR decisions.
nodes.norm_label: tests/graph - the graph and the always-on context tier

nodes.label: tests/capabilities - The Seams a Feature Arrives Through
nodes.rationale: 19 files, 291 tests over ADBC, artifacts, tools, toolkits, warehouse scope, quack, dlt runtime and workflow runs.
nodes.norm_label: tests/capabilities - the seams a feature arrives through

nodes.label: tests/ontology - What Things Mean and What Must Hold

nodes.label: Anomaly Tests Warn, Built-Ins Error
nodes.rationale: A key that is not unique is a broken model; a row count 3 sigma low is a question. Severity is how the two stay distinguishable, and a run where everything is error gets ignored wholesale the first busy week. An anomaly test must never gate a merge - it reports on data and the merge gate judges code.

nodes.label: REST API Pipeline Skill
nodes.rationale: Use the declarative rest_api source before writing any request code, and reach for RESTClient only for a shape it cannot express - parallel arrays are the case for a Python parser, not for a selector. Name the paginator: detection is for exploring, not for a source of record. A load that left a table empty is red, not done.

nodes.label: Per-Key Cursors in Resource State
nodes.rationale: dlt incremental is one cursor per resource; when the window is per key, one series per symbol, keep a cursor per key in dlt.current.resource_state() instead. State syncs with the destination and is dropped when the dataset is gone, so a wiped warehouse rebackfills.
nodes.community_name: Platform Docs — Commodity End To End

nodes.label: DEFAULT_CONTRACT (data_type freeze)
nodes.rationale: The platform applies it to every source; tighten to STRICT_CONTRACT per source, never loosen. Failure isolation differs by role: a backup feed ignores 429 and 5xx per request, a source of record raises when every request failed.
